NUZZLE.scope: The five units in appliesTo declare NUZZLE in this production reference. The strategy is shared; the unit-specific differences are only the star count (table index), the passive and the stats. Pachirisu's own passive (Passive.PACHIRISU) is NOT covered here (see passiveGaps).
NUZZLE.summary: Moves the caster to a free cell next to an enemy chosen by Board.getFarthestTargetCoordinateAvailablePlace (usually far from the caster, but NOT guaranteed to be the farthest enemy: see targeting), retargets to that enemy, then paralyses it and deals special damage. If the helper returns null the caster stays and hits the cast target.

targeting.who: the enemy attached to the helper's selected cell: scanning enemies in board order, each enemy whose distance is STRICTLY greater than the running maximum updates the maximum and, only if it has at least one free adjacent cell, replaces the selected destination (and its enemy). The cast target is replaced by that enemy.
targeting.note: Cases (read from the helper, not executed): (1) normal: the last maximum-setting enemy that has a free adjacent cell is chosen, with the free adjacent cell farthest from the caster (first such cell on ties). (2) RETAINED SELECTION: if an enemy that sets a new maximum distance has no free adjacent cell, the earlier selectedCell is kept (it is never cleared) and its enemy - nearer than the farthest - becomes the target. (3) because the running maximum was already raised, enemies scanned later at a distance <= that maximum are skipped, even if they are nearer than the farthest enemy but farther than the retained one, and even if they have free cells. (4) FALLBACK: only if no enemy at all produced a selected cell, the free cell closest to the last-recorded 'farthest' enemy (getClosestAvailablePlace) is used with that enemy as target. (5) if that also fails (or no targettable enemy exists) the helper returns null: the caster does not move and the original cast target is hit. Ties in distance keep the first enemy in scan order (strict >). The scan order of board.forEach and the exact distanceM metric were not read.

geometry.shape: single target; caster relocates to the free adjacent cell (of the selected enemy) that is farthest from the caster, first on ties; unchanged if no cell is returned

effects.scaling: AP: damage x (1 + AP/100) (apBoost true is passed); the cast's crit flag multiplies by critPower only if the cast crit (needs ABILITY_CRIT: canCritByDefault is false)
effects.resolution: then the target's SPE_DEF division (damage / (1 + 0.05 x SPE_DEF), ceil, min 1) and later untraced modifiers; blocked entirely by protect / skydiving / magicBounce

statusEffects.scaling: none from AP (triggerParalysis apBoost defaults to false and is not passed); not crit-scaled
statusEffects.applicationOrder: paralysis is applied BEFORE the damage call in the source
statusEffects.guards: not applied if runeProtect or IMMUNITY_PARALYSIS; storm weather x1.3 (Electric Quartz lowers it); aquatic/Odd Keystone reductions via applyStatusDurationReductions; a new paralysis only replaces the remaining time if it is longer
statusEffects.combatEffect: while paralysed the target's speed counts as half in the attack interval and in move speed, and it cannot dodge basic attacks. Uses of paralysis found in attacking-state.ts, move-speed.ts, pokemon-state.ts and pokemon-entity.ts are these three; other files were not searched.

starBehavior.note: indexed by the casting entity's stars; the 4-star column (200 damage, 6000 ms) is not reachable by any of the five units' bare factory star counts (stars are 1, 2, 3, 3, 3). Whether other mechanics raise an entity's star count was not examined.

NUZZLE.positionalConditions: Needs at least one targettable enemy. The destination is the helper's selected cell: normally next to the last maximum-setting enemy that has a free adjacent cell; an earlier, nearer selection is retained when a farther enemy has no free adjacent cell, and later nearer enemies are then skipped; the closest-free-cell fallback is used only when no enemy produced a selected cell; if nothing is found, no move and the original target is hit (see targeting.note).
NUZZLE.repeatedCastsAndModes: No stored state: each cast re-runs the helper on the current board, jumps, paralyses and hits. No modes. Two casts on the same target extend paralysis only if the new duration exceeds the remaining one.
NUZZLE.rawVsResolved: Declared raw: damage 25/50/100 (1/2/3 stars) and paralysis 3000 ms for 1-3 stars. The damage dealt is the raw value x (1 + AP/100), then SPE_DEF division (ceil, at least 1) and untraced modifiers; the paralysis length is the raw value after the listed status modifiers.

DRAGON_RAGE.scope: Gyarados only (the single catalog unit with this skill). DRAGON_RAGE is used by no other registry entry and the effect flag EffectEnum.DRAGON_RAGE appears only in dragon-rage.ts in the server code (grep over app/*.ts; client animation files excluded).
DRAGON_RAGE.summary: Gives the caster an initial shield and starts a 6-pulse effect: each pulse (every 1000 timer units) adds more shield and hits all adjacent enemies with special damage; when the effect ends, C = min(current shield, tracked raw shield) is removed from the shield and 40 % of C (rounded) is requested as healing.

targeting.who: no target needed (castable anywhere); pulses hit adjacent enemies of the caster

geometry.shape: the 8 cells adjacent to the caster's current position, re-read at each pulse (the caster may have moved)

effects.condition: each pulse, to every enemy on an adjacent cell
effects.scaling: AP: x(1 + AP/100) (no apBoost argument => handleSpecialDamage default true); crit only if the cast itself crit (needs ABILITY_CRIT), and that crit flag is stored in the effect at creation
effects.resolution: then SPE_DEF division per pulse, ceil, min 1, and later modifiers

effects.condition: once on the first cast (initial) and once per pulse
effects.scaling: addShield(value, caster, apBoost 1, crit): x(1 + AP/100), x critPower if the cast crit, halved if the unit is enraged, rounded; Big Eater Belt hook in PokemonEntity.addShield
effects.resolution: the amount actually received can exceed (AP) or fall below (enrage) the raw value, while the stored counter `shieldGiven` adds the RAW value only

effects.condition: when the effect ends (7th timer fire) or when the ability is cast again while active; C = min(current shield, shieldGiven)

declaredRaw.formula: removes C shield; requests healing round(0.4 x C), where C = min(current shield, shieldGiven)
declaredRaw.note: removed shield (C) and requested healing (0.4 x C, rounded) are different amounts. shieldGiven = raw initial shield + raw per-pulse shields added since the effect (or since the last conversion) started

perUnitRaw.GYARADOS: C = 135 gives 135 shield removed and a base healing request of round(0.4 x 135) = 54 (before healing modifiers); other values of C give other amounts

effects.scaling: the healing request is not AP- or crit-scaled (handleHeal called with apBoost 0, crit false), but handleHeal then applies its own modifiers: wound => 0, burn x0.5, enraged x0.5, BUFF_HEAL_RECEIVED x1.3, zenith weather x1.2, rounding, cap at missing HP. The 54 is the BASE request, not a universal maximum: modifiers can raise or lower the healing received, and C itself varies (damage taken, recast, enrage)
effects.resolution: C depends on how much of the tracked shield is still on the unit; the removal is an exchange (shield lost) while the healing request is 40 % of it; actual healing received is whatever handleHeal returns

starBehavior.note: indexed by the casting entity's stars: Gyarados (3 stars) uses initial 45, per-pulse shield 15, per-pulse damage 15. The 1/2/4-star columns are listed as the table's content only.

DRAGON_RAGE.positionalConditions: None for casting. Damage depends on which enemies are on the 8 adjacent cells at each pulse.
DRAGON_RAGE.repeatedCastsAndModes: State: a DragonRageEffect with ticksRemaining (6) and shieldGiven. FIRST cast: adds the initial shield and creates the effect. CAST WHILE ACTIVE: no new initial shield is added; the active effect converts its tracked shield into healing right away (consumeShield) and ticksRemaining is reset to 6 (the effect's 1000-unit timer is not reset). The effect ends on the pulse where ticksRemaining would go below 0, i.e. after 6 damaging pulses the 7th timer fire ends it and converts what is left. Each cast still spends maxPP of PP.
DRAGON_RAGE.rawVsResolved: Declared raw for 3 stars: initial shield 45, per pulse shield 15 and damage 15, 6 pulses; tracked raw shield 45 + 6 x 15 = 135. With C = 135 (all tracked shield still present at the end) the conversion removes 135 shield and requests round(0.4 x 135) = 54 healing as the BASE request, before handleHeal's modifiers (burn/enrage halve, wound zeroes, BUFF_HEAL_RECEIVED x1.3, zenith x1.2) and the cap at missing HP. Actual shield received includes AP scaling and may be lower after damage, so C can be smaller; it can never exceed the tracked raw counter.

one pulse on one adjacent enemy with SPE_DEF 10, AP 0, no crit, no shield: ceil(15 / 1.5) = 10; six pulses = 60 only if the enemy stays adjacent, alive and unshielded for all six

THRASH.scope: Mankey, Primeape and Annihilape (all declare THRASH in this production reference). The strategy is shared; stars select the attack multiplier, and baseAtk is read from the entity, so a Primeape's value depends on its permanent attack. Primeape's passive PRIMEAPE is a separate record (passives.PRIMEAPE).
THRASH.summary: Self-buff: adds attack equal to a star-dependent percentage of the unit's base attack, then confuses the caster itself for 3000 ms (not refreshed while already confused). No enemy is targeted and no damage is dealt by the cast.

targeting.who: the caster only; no target needed

effects.scaling: addAttack(value, caster, apBoost 1, crit): value x (1 + AP/100) x (critPower if the cast crit), rounded, then Big Eater / Twist Band hooks (Twist Band is a no-op for a positive self buff); ATK floor 1
effects.resolution: baseAtk is the entity's ATK at creation (the board Pokemon's atk, which includes earlier permanent attack); the buff is NOT permanent (permanent defaults to false) and has no expiry timer in the ability code, so it lasts for the fight

statusEffects.scaling: none (triggerConfusion apBoost defaults to false and is not passed)
statusEffects.guards: not applied if the unit is already confused (so a recast during confusion does NOT extend it), runeProtect, or IMMUNITY_CONFUSION (e.g. after Persim Berry); sandstorm x1.3; reductions through applyStatusDurationReductions; a Persim Berry holder eats it
statusEffects.combatEffect: while confused, every basic-attack target selection is replaced: with a 50 % (luck-adjusted) roll the unit keeps normal enemy targeting among the nearest in range+1, otherwise allies are also eligible, the nearest is picked and the unit itself is added as a candidate; when confusion ends the target is cleared. This code is in the attacking state; the moving state has no confusion branch in the lines searched. Ability casting does not need a target for THRASH.

starBehavior.note: 1 and 2 stars share 100 %; 3 stars is 120 %; the 150 % entry is unreachable by these three units' bare star counts. Absolute values depend on baseAtk: 7 / 20 / 30 on the bare catalog instances.

THRASH.positionalConditions: None. The cast has no range or target requirement; the self-confusion affects who the unit attacks afterwards.
THRASH.repeatedCastsAndModes: Each cast adds another ATK increment computed from the same baseAtk (the increments stack within the fight, with no cap in the ability). The confusion is only (re)applied when the unit is not confused, so casts closer together than 3000 ms (plus any lengthening) do not extend it. No modes.
THRASH.rawVsResolved: Declared raw: attack + floor(percent/100 x baseAtk), then x(1 + AP/100) and rounding; Mankey +7 and Primeape +20 (bare baseAtk), Annihilape +36 (120 % of 30). Confusion 3000 ms before duration modifiers.

DIVE.scope: Lapras (3 stars, maxPP 120), Wailmer (1 star, maxPP 100) and Wailord (2 stars, maxPP 100) declare ABILITY DIVE (range 1, no passive). Similarly named abilities (GRUDGE_DIVE, TRIPLE_DIVE, the skydiving status) are separate and not covered.
DIVE.summary: Destination, self shield, relocation and adjacent burst. The strategy first computes the destination: the empty cell with the most adjacent opposing-team units (the first of the sorted list on ties; no destination is returned only if no cell is empty). Only then does it give the caster a flat shield (15/30/60/120 by stars, requested; no AP or crit scaling because apBoost 0 and crit false are passed; Big Eater Belt x1.25 and enrage x0.5 do apply). The shield is added whether or not a destination exists. If a destination exists the caster then moves there (moveTo, not a forced displacement) and deals flat SPECIAL damage (10/20/40/80 by stars, requested, with AP and crit scaling) to every enemy in the 8 cells adjacent to the new position. Without an empty cell the shield is still granted but there is no movement and no damage. requiresTarget is false, so the cast does not need a target in range.

targeting.who: the caster (shield); every enemy unit in the up-to-8 cells adjacent to the destination cell (damage)
targeting.note: The destination is chosen from empty cells by the number of adjacent units of the opponent team, not from the cast target. The target parameter is null-typed and unused.

geometry.shape: destination = empty cell with the maximum count of adjacent opponent units (getAdjacentCells, 8-neighbourhood); damage area = the 8 cells adjacent to the destination, centre excluded
geometry.detail: The candidate list is built over the whole board in board.forEach order, sorted by neighbour count descending with Array.prototype.sort and the first entry is taken, so ties keep the earlier cell in board order (stable sort). Counting is against opponentTeam only. Cells off the board are skipped. The adjacency used for damage is computed after the move, from the caster's new position. The destination is computed before the shield is added; the shield does not change the choice.

effects.scaling: Requested amount = table value. pokemon.addShield(shield, pokemon, 0, false): apBoost 0 means no AP multiplier and crit false means no crit multiplier, so the caster's AP does not change it. Applied amount: applyBigEaterBeltStatBuff multiplies by 1.25 (rounded down, 0 digits) when the caster holds Big Eater Belt (value > 0); state.addShield halves it while the caster is enraged, then rounds and adds it to pokemon.shield (floored at 0); nothing is added if the caster's hp is not above 0.
effects.resolution: Requested 15/30/60/120 -> applied after Big Eater Belt and enrage as described; the shield is granted after the destination lookup and before the move, independent of whether a destination exists. Twist Band does not apply (it only flips negative values).

While paralysed, the attack-cooldown and movement-speed formulas use half of the caster's stored speed (the stored stat is unchanged) and the caster cannot dodge basic attacks. The self-paralysis is skipped if the caster has runeProtect or IMMUNITY_PARALYSIS, but the single-target damage is requested regardless: it does not depend on the self-paralysis result.

FAKE_TEARS.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
FAKE_TEARS.scope: The three units in appliesTo (Gothita 1 star, Gothorita 2, Gothitelle 3) declare FAKE_TEARS; maxPP 80 and range 3 for all. Gothita and Gothorita declare passive HATCH in the catalog and Gothitelle none; HATCH is not covered here. The strategy is shared; unit differences are the star count (table index).
FAKE_TEARS.summary: Hits EVERY enemy unit on the board (every occupied cell whose unit is not on the caster's team; no range or target limit), not just the cast target. For each enemy, in board-iteration order, it first calls triggerArmorReduction(3000 ms for 1-3 stars) on that enemy and then requests SPECIAL damage (raw 5/10/15 by the caster's stars) from it. Rune Protect on an enemy's own status refuses the NEW armor-reduction application on that enemy, but that alone does not make its current armorReduction flag false: the damage step reads the flag as it is when the hit is processed. A successful application sets the flag before the damage, so the halved SPE_DEF applies to this same hit; a refused one leaves the flag as it was (false if the enemy had no earlier armor reduction, so its normal SPE_DEF applies; true if an earlier one is still flagged, because clearNegativeStatus zeroes the cooldown but not the boolean). The duration reductions (Swift Swim, Hydration, Water Veil / Surge Surfer, Odd Keystone) read the enemy that was passed as the entity argument, i.e. the TARGET of each application, not the caster. Protect, skydiving and magicBounce on an enemy are not cleared and block that enemy's damage (the armor reduction is still applied); a magicBounce enemy also queues a delayed SPECIAL bounce at the caster unless the caster holds Protective Pads.

targeting.note: requiresTarget is the base default true, so the caster needs a target at range to reach the cast gate (only the pp >= maxPP && canCast gate was read); once cast, the loop ignores that target and reaches the whole board.

effects.resolution: requested amount per enemy = raw x AP factor [x crit]. Per enemy, handleDamage uses Math.round(speDef / 2) whenever that enemy's current armorReduction flag is true when the hit is processed (a successful application sets it just before; a Rune-Protect-refused application leaves the flag unchanged, so with no earlier flag the full SPE_DEF is used). The division is an intermediate calculation (ceil, min 1) and later untraced modifiers follow, so it is not the final HP loss; takenDamage (not used by this strategy, the return value is discarded) would count HP removed plus shield damage. An enemy with protect, skydiving or magicBounce takes 0 from the hit (the armor reduction on it is still applied first). The hit applies once per enemy, so the total across the board scales with the number of enemies.

statusEffects.applicationOrder: per enemy: armor reduction first, then that enemy's damage
statusEffects.guards: a new application is refused for an enemy whose status has runeProtect (checked on the status the method is called on, i.e. that enemy's); the refusal neither sets nor clears the flag and does not cancel that enemy's damage. A refused application (Rune Protect) does not prove the enemy's CURRENT armorReduction flag is false: the damage step reads the flag as it is when the hit is processed. triggerRuneProtect calls clearNegativeStatus, which zeroes armorReductionCooldown but not the boolean, so a flag set before Rune Protect appeared stays true until updateArmorReduction runs; with no earlier flag, a refused application leaves the normal defenses in place. When applied, the duration goes through applyStatusDurationReductions(duration, pkm) where pkm is the ENEMY itself (value, supplied as the entity argument): if that enemy has SWIFT_SWIM the duration is x0.7, else HYDRATION x0.5, else WATER_VEIL / SURGE_SURFER x0.3 (Math.round), and each Odd Keystone in that enemy's player's items takes a further 10 % off. So, unlike RAGING_BULL (which passes the caster), the reductions come from the enemy being hit and the caster's own abilities/items do not shorten it. A new application replaces the remaining time only if longer. These reductions were read in the source; the pinned helper was not executed in this run.

KING_SHIELD.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
KING_SHIELD.scope: Four units declare KING_SHIELD: Honedge (1 star), Doublade (2 stars), Aegislash and Aegislash Blade (3 stars, both with passive AEGISLASH). The strategy is shared; the form-change branch only runs for units whose passive is AEGISLASH.
KING_SHIELD.summary: The caster gains protect for 1500 ms (if it is not already protected and not enraged) and a self shield of 10/20/40/80 by stars (requested; applied after Big Eater Belt, AP, crit, enraged halving and rounding). It then swaps cells with the farthest targettable enemy (forced displacement, so it does nothing if either side cannot be moved). Units with passive AEGISLASH also toggle form after 1500 ms: Aegislash becomes Blade (requested +10 attack, -5 DEF, -5 SPE_DEF) and Blade returns to Aegislash (requested reverse). The applied amounts depend on Big Eater Belt, which also scales negative changes the holder causes to itself, so the two directions need not cancel (see the statChange effect).

effects.resolution: the requested amounts go through the stat adders. applyBigEaterBeltStatBuff first multiplies by 1.25 and rounds with mode 'down' (Math.floor) when the value is positive OR when it is negative and comes from a caster on the holder's own team (here the holder itself): for a Big Eater Belt holder +10 becomes +12, -5 becomes -7, +5 becomes +6 and -10 becomes -13 (floor of a negative number goes further from zero). applyTwistBandBuff then changes only negative values from another team or the environment, so it does nothing here. Floors afterwards: attack at least 1, DEF and SPE_DEF at least 0. Pinned-helper probe (AP 0, no crit, no floor reached; holder ATK / DEF / SPE_DEF 30 / 20 / 20): without the belt Aegislash->Blade gives 40 / 15 / 15 and Blade->Aegislash returns to 30 / 20 / 20; with Big Eater Belt Aegislash->Blade gives 42 / 13 / 13 and Blade->Aegislash gives 29 / 19 / 19, so the inverse changes do not cancel (net -1 ATK, -1 DEF, -1 SPE_DEF per round trip). LEECH_SEED.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
LEECH_SEED.scope: Four units declare LEECH_SEED: Shroomish (1 star), Breloom (2 stars), Lileep (1 star) and Cradily (2 stars); none declares a passive. The strategy is shared; differences are the star index, maxPP and range.
LEECH_SEED.summary: The caster heals itself by 20/40/80/160 (requested; by stars, with AP and crit scaling) and applies one poison stack to the cast target for 3000/6000/12000/24000 ms (requested; by stars). The cast heal is a fixed self-heal of the CASTER; it is not tied to damage dealt by the poison. Separately, Status.updatePoison computes a signed amount on each poison tick (5% of the poisoned unit's max HP per stack, passed through the listed multipliers and rounded): a negative result calls handleHeal on the POISONED unit, zero makes no call, and a positive result requests TRUE damage on the poisoned unit attributed to the poison origin. These are handler requests, not guaranteed final HP changes: a wound blocks the HP heal (for the caster's self-heal and for a negative poison tick alike) but does not guarantee 'no effect', because the shared Blood Moon / Blood Stone branch can request a compensating shield first.

FLAME_CHARGE.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
FLAME_CHARGE.scope: The four units in appliesTo declare FLAME_CHARGE in this production reference. The strategy is shared; differences are star count and stats.
FLAME_CHARGE.summary: The caster dashes to the destination returned by Board.getFarthestTargetCoordinateAvailablePlace and deals SPECIAL damage (raw 30/60/120/240 by caster stars) once to every enemy on the cells of the line between its starting cell and that destination. The destination is NOT guaranteed to be next to the farthest enemy: the helper can retain a cell chosen for an earlier, nearer enemy (see positionalConditions). If the line holds no enemy only the cast target is hit; if the helper returns null the caster does not move and only the cast target is hit.

targeting.who: every enemy standing on the cells between the caster and the destination; the destination comes from the helper's scan of targettable enemies, not from the cast target
targeting.note: requiresTarget is the base default true, so a target in range is needed to cast; the target is used only as the fallback victim. isTargettableBy (which enemies count) was not read. The helper's selection rule is described in positionalConditions.

effects.target: each distinct enemy on the line (a Set, so one hit per enemy), or only the cast target if none
effects.scaling: AP: damage x (1 + AP/100) (apBoost defaults to true); the crit flag multiplies by critPower (reduced by the target's crit reduction) only if the cast rolled a crit (needs ABILITY_CRIT because canCritByDefault is false)
effects.resolution: requested = the raw amount; applied = after AP/crit, the target's SPE_DEF division (damage / (1 + 0.05 x SPE_DEF), ceil, min 1) and later untraced modifiers; a target with protect / skydiving / magicBounce takes none. The strategy does not read takenDamage.

effects.scaling: none
effects.resolution: moveTo(destination, forced displacement false) after the line cells were collected; it swaps the caster with whatever occupies the destination (normally nothing, since the destination is a free cell). The damage is dealt after the move to the enemies collected before it. The destination is next to the farthest enemy only when that enemy had a free adjacent cell; otherwise see positionalConditions.

starBehavior.note: indexed by the casting entity's stars; the 4-star value (240, also the fallback) is not reachable by the units' bare star counts. maxPP and range are in appliesTo.

FLAME_CHARGE.positionalConditions: Selection in board.ts:568-630 (same helper as NUZZLE and AQUA_JET): board.forEach scans cells row by row (y outer, x inner); only targettable enemies whose Manhattan distance from the caster is STRICTLY greater than the running maximum are considered, so equal distances keep the first one scanned and enemies up to the running maximum are skipped afterwards. When such an enemy is found the running cell maximum is reset to 0 and its free adjacent cells (getAdjacentCells order) are compared by distance from the caster, the first strictly farther one winning; selectedCell is replaced only when that enemy has at least one free adjacent cell. If it has none, selectedCell is NOT cleared and keeps the cell chosen for an earlier, nearer enemy, whose enemy then counts as the target of the destination. The fallback (the free cell closest by Manhattan distance to the farthest enemy found, anywhere on the board, which may not be adjacent) runs only if selectedCell is still null at the end. Pinned-helper probe on a 6-row x 8-column board, caster (0,0): near enemy (2,0), far enemy (7,5) boxed in by three allies -> destination (3,1) next to the NEAR enemy; far enemy with a free neighbour -> destination (7,4) next to the far enemy; far enemy as the only enemy and boxed in -> fallback cell (7,3). If it returns null (no targettable enemy or no free cell) the caster does not move and only the cast target is hit.

SLUDGE.scope: The four units in appliesTo declare SLUDGE in this production reference (all with passive NONE in the catalog, maxPP 100, range 1). The strategy is shared; differences are star count (1 or 2) and stats.
SLUDGE.summary: Applies poison to every enemy standing in the three cells directly in front of the caster (towards its target). For each such enemy the strategy makes nbStacks successive triggerPoison calls (2/3/4/8 by stars: 1 star = 2, 2 stars = 3) with a duration of 3000/3000/3000/10000 ms scaled by AP (and critPower only if the cast crit). Each call adds one stack up to a cap of 3 (4 if the caster has VENOMOUS, 5 with TOXIC). So from zero stacks and without reactions a 1-star cast requests and applies 2 stacks and a 2-star cast requests and applies 3; among the 1-3-star requests only the 3-star request (4) exceeds the base cap of 3 (it applies 3, or 4 with VENOMOUS); the declared four-star / fallback request of 8 also exceeds the base cap, but the listed units are 1- and 2-star in the catalog and no four-star availability is claimed here. The calls are not one atomic addition: immunity, Rune Protect and berry reactions are evaluated in each call (a Pecha Berry holder eats the berry during the first call, which clears the stacks and grants poison immunity, so the later calls do nothing). No direct damage. The poison then ticks about every 1000 ms: a negative computed amount requests a heal on the poisoned unit itself (reachable through the Gliscor formula), zero makes no call, a positive amount requests TRUE damage attributed to the poison origin; these are handler requests, not guaranteed HP changes.

VOLT_SWITCH.summary: The caster moves to the destination returned by Board.getFarthestTargetCoordinateAvailablePlace, which is NOT guaranteed to be next to the farthest targettable enemy: a cell selected for an earlier, nearer enemy survives when a later, farther enemy has no free neighbour, and the fallback to the free cell closest to the farthest enemy runs only if no cell was ever selected. Before moving, every enemy standing on the straight (supercover) line between the caster's start cell and that destination is collected; each takes SPECIAL damage (raw 25/50/100/200 by stars) after the move. If the hit set is empty (nobody on the line, or no destination) the cast target is hit instead. The crit flag is the cast's crit, rolled only with ABILITY_CRIT.

The fallback (the free cell closest to the farthest enemy found, anywhere on the board) runs only if selectedCell is still null. FLOWER_TRICK.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
FLOWER_TRICK.scope: The three units in appliesTo declare FLOWER_TRICK: Sprigatito (1 star), Floragato (2) and Meowscarada (3); maxPP 100, range 2 and passive NONE for all in the catalog. The strategy is shared; unit differences are the star count (damage table index).
FLOWER_TRICK.summary: Delayed area hit around the cast target. At cast time the strategy only records how many crits the cast target has received so far (its crit counter) and queues a command on the caster that runs 3000 ms later (on the first update after the delay has elapsed). When it runs it takes the difference between the target's crit counter now and at cast time (the counter does NOT count only successful crit hits; its semantics follow below) and takes the 3x3 block centred on the target's position AT THAT TIME (centre included) and gives every enemy unit in it SPECIAL damage of (raw 15/40/85 by the caster's stars + 15 per counted crit), AP-scaled and crit-multiplied only if the original cast crit. The crit bonus is added to the raw amount, so AP scaling applies to it too. The target is the unit fixed at cast time; it need not be alive or in the same cell, and the explosion is centred on its last known position. Nothing is dealt at cast time. Crit counter semantics: PokemonState.attack increments target.count.crit whenever a basic attack's crit roll succeeds, unless the target holds Rocky Helmet, BEFORE the dodge and protect checks, so a dodged or protected crit roll still counts although the attack dealt nothing. PokemonEntity.handleSpecialDamage increments it for a crit ability hit only after the protect / skydiving / magicBounce block, and Rocky Helmet suppresses it for non-TRUE damage only, so a TRUE ability crit still increments it. Pinned-helper probe: a forced crit that is dodged leaves basic damage 0 and raises the counter by 1, and a one-star Flower Trick then requests raw 30 instead of 15; with a Rocky Helmet, raw 10, AP 0 and critPower 2, a TRUE crit increments the counter and hands 20 to the damage handler while a SPECIAL crit leaves the counter at 0 and hands 10.

targeting.who: all enemy units in the 3x3 block around the cast target's position at the moment the delayed command runs, the target included if it is still there
targeting.note: requiresTarget is the base default true; the delayed command holds the target object and reads its position when it fires.

effects.scaling: requested raw = table value + 15 x numberOfCrits; AP: x (1 + AP/100) per enemy (apBoost default true) read from the caster when the command runs; the cast's crit flag (from cast time) multiplies by critPower (reduced by each enemy's critReductionFactor) only if that cast crit, which requires EffectEnum.ABILITY_CRIT because canCritByDefault is false
effects.resolution: numberOfCrits = target.count.crit at fire time minus its value at cast time. The counter rises (a) in PokemonState.attack whenever a basic attack's crit roll succeeds and the target has no Rocky Helmet, before the dodge and protect checks (so dodged or protected crit rolls count); (b) in PokemonEntity.handleSpecialDamage for a crit ability hit that passed the protect / skydiving / magicBounce block, except that Rocky Helmet suppresses it for non-TRUE damage only (a TRUE crit still counts). It counts every source and every such increment on that target in the window. Per enemy: SPE_DEF division (ceil, min 1) and untraced later modifiers, so it is an intermediate calculation, not the final HP loss; takenDamage (not used, the return value is discarded) would count HP removed plus shield damage. Blocked entirely by protect / skydiving / magicBounce on that enemy at fire time (takes 0; the explosion animation is still broadcast); a magicBounce enemy also queues a delayed SPECIAL bounce at the caster unless it holds Protective Pads. Requested vs applied: the table value (15/40/85) is the minimum raw; the crit bonus can only raise it.

DARKEST_LARIAT.scope: INCINEROAR, LITTEN and TORRACAT (the queued units; none has a passive in the catalog). The strategy is shared; the units differ in stars and stats only.
DARKEST_LARIAT.summary: Single-target multi-hit SPECIAL damage. The target is flinched for a requested 1000 ms, and round((1 + 0.01 x speed) x 3) hits (speed read at cast time) are queued as delayed commands at delays round(i x 1000 / hits) ms; each requests 1 x the caster's ATK (read at that hit; 2 x at 4 stars) as SPECIAL damage. Each callback tests the stored target's hp > 0 when it enters. Fire-synergy effects (WILDFIRE +1, BLAZE +2, DESOLATE_LAND +3, first match only) add attack to the caster AFTER the damage request of every callback that passed that hp test, even when the request was blocked (protect / skydiving / magicBounce, takenDamage 0) or dealt nothing, and even when it killed the target; a callback whose target already has hp 0 on entry makes neither request nor gain (pinned-strategy probe: WILDFIRE, ATK 30, blocked damage -> ATK 31 after the first callback). The caster then moves to the empty cell closest, by Manhattan distance and over the whole board, to the point target + (target - caster): the FULL vector from the caster to the target applied again from the target, not one sign-step past it; the point may lie off the board.

targeting.who: the cast target passed to the strategy (the caster's current target); every queued hit goes to that same target

DRAGON_BREATH.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
DRAGON_BREATH.scope: Gible (1 star), Gabite (2 stars) and Garchomp (3 stars), all Dragon/Ground/Monster, maxPP 100, range 1, no passive, declare ABILITY DRAGON_BREATH.
DRAGON_BREATH.summary: Directional breath. Deals flat SPECIAL damage (requested 25/50/100/200 by stars) to every enemy-team unit on the cells walked by effectInOrientation from the caster in one of 8 directions, limited to Chebyshev distance range + 1 = 2 from the caster. The direction is chosen by the sign of the target's offset (dx, dy), not an exact line to the target. Known helper exception: for RIGHT the loop is `x < board.rows` (6) although the production board has 8 columns and 6 rows, so the nominal two-cell ray is shortened: from a caster in column 3 or lower both cells are walked, from column 4 only column 5, from column 5 or beyond nothing. If no enemy is found on the walked cells (including when nothing is walked) the cast target itself is hit once by the helper's fallback; if an enemy was found, the fallback adds no extra hit (probe: caster (4,2), range 1, enemies (5,2) and (6,2), RIGHT -> only (5,2) receives a damage request).

targeting.who: every enemy-team unit (team different from the caster) on the walked cells within distance 2 in one of 8 directions; fallback: the cast target
targeting.note: Direction = board.orientation(caster, target): sign of dx and dy, so a target at a non-axis, non-45-degree offset yields a diagonal that may not contain it. The walk starts at the cell after the caster and runs to the board edge, but applyEffect skips cells whose Chebyshev distance to the caster is above maxRange (2). Allies are never damaged: the strategy's callback tests team !== caster team. The RIGHT case loops x < board.rows (6) although the board has 8 columns (see the BLAZE_KICK record), so a RIGHT-facing cast never visits columns 6 and 7: from a caster in column 4 only column 5 is reached, and from column 5 or beyond nothing is walked (the fallback then hits the cast target).

geometry.shape: ray of up to 2 cells in one of 8 directions from the caster (not a cone and not width 3); for RIGHT on the 8-column board the ray stops at column 5 (x < board.rows = 6)
geometry.detail: Cells at distance 1 and 2 along the direction are visited, in order; cells beyond are skipped by the maxRange check (the loop continues to the edge but does nothing). maxRange is pokemon.range + 1 and range is 1 for all three units, so 2. The fallback hits the target even if it lay outside the ray. RIGHT is the exception: its loop bound is board.rows (6), not board.columns (8), so columns 6 and 7 are never visited; the walked cells are columns caster+1 and caster+2 only while they are at most 5. LEFT and the other directions use the real bounds.

effects.target: each enemy on the walked cells (or the cast target by fallback)
effects.scaling: Requested amount = table value. handleSpecialDamage(damage, board, SPECIAL, caster, crit) with the default apBoost = true: damage + damage x AP/100, then x2 if the caster has DOUBLE_DAMAGE (consumed once per hit instance), x1.2 with the strange-steam board effect, then the crit multiplier only if the cast crit (needs ABILITY_CRIT; canCritByDefault false). Each enemy receives one instance.
effects.resolution: Requested 25/50/100 is pre-defence. The target's special defence enters an intermediate division (damage / (1 + 0.05 x speDef), rounded up, minimum 1) that is not guaranteed final HP damage; shield damage counts in takenDamage (core-mechanics.md section A). Blocked by protect, skydiving, magicBounce (magicBounce reflects). The same per-enemy request is made whether the enemy was reached by the ray or by the fallback.

starBehavior.note: Caster stars index the damage table (1-4, fallback 200). Range stays 1, so the reach is always 2 cells.

DRAGON_BREATH.positionalConditions: Enemies are hit only if they stand on the walked cells of the chosen direction within distance 2 (for RIGHT, only columns up to 5). If no enemy is found on the walked cells, only the cast target is hit (the helper's fallback), including when the target stands outside the shortened RIGHT ray or at a diagonal-ish offset; when at least one enemy was found the target gets no extra hit.
DRAGON_BREATH.rawVsResolved: Requested: 25/50/100 special damage per enemy for 1/2/3 stars. Applied: AP percentage, DOUBLE_DAMAGE, strange steam and crit raise it before the target's special defence and shield; taken damage includes shield-absorbed damage, minimum 1 per hit. Which enemies receive a request depends on the walked cells: a RIGHT cast stops at column 5, and the cast target alone is requested when no enemy was found.

DRUM_BEATING.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
DRUM_BEATING.scope: The three units in appliesTo declare DRUM_BEATING: Grookey (1 star), Thwackey (2 stars), Rillaboom (3 stars), all with the DRUMMER passive and maxPP 60. Units not listed are not covered. The DRUMMER passive (PP for adjacent allies when drumming instead of attacking) is a different mechanism and is not covered here.
DRUM_BEATING.summary: Cycles through three modes by the caster's cast counter. count.ult is incremented in the base process BEFORE the switch reads it, so with count.ult starting at 0 the 1st cast (ult=1) is the shield mode, the 2nd (ult=2) the damage mode, the 3rd (ult=3, 3%3=0) the speed mode, then repeating. Speed: +10/20/40 speed (requested) to every ally on the board including the caster. Shield: 10/20/40 (requested) shield to every ally including the caster. Damage: 10/20/40 (requested) SPECIAL damage to every enemy on the board. The 80 column is the 4-star / fallback value.

targeting.who: speed and shield modes: all entities whose team equals the caster's, found by scanning the whole board (caster included, no range limit); damage mode: all entities whose team differs from the caster's
targeting.note: requiresTarget is true by default so the caster must reach a target to cast, but the cast target itself is not used by the strategy; effects are board-wide.

geometry.shape: whole board; no area, range or line

effects.target: every ally on the board, caster included
effects.scaling: PokemonEntity.addSpeed (apBoost 1): first item-helper pass: Big Eater Belt x1.25 rounded down on the holder (positive value), Twist Band irrelevant (positive). Ordinary ally: then x (1 + AP/100) x critPower if the cast crit, with no rounding, added to speed and clamped to 0..300. MELMETAL-passive ally: instead addAttack(belted value x 0.5, caster, apBoost 1, crit); addAttack rounds Math.round(v x (1 + AP/100) x critPower if the cast crit), then applies Big Eater Belt a SECOND time and Twist Band, then atk = max(1, atk + v). Pinned-helper probe (raw 10, Melmetal with Big Eater Belt, AP 0, no crit): first pass 12, delegated Attack value 6, second pass 7; Attack rises by 7 and the stored speed is unchanged.
effects.resolution: applied = value added to the ally's current speed, clamped to 0..300 (MAX_SPEED); requested and applied differ for allies near the cap and with Big Eater Belt. For a Melmetal-passive ally nothing is added to speed: its Attack rises by the double-belted, rounded half (7 in the probe case) and its stored speed is unchanged. Not permanent. The caster's AP/crit are used for every ally.

effects.target: every ally on the board, caster included
effects.scaling: PokemonEntity.addShield: Big Eater Belt on the receiving ally's positive value (x1.25 rounded down); PokemonState.addShield with apBoost 1: x (1 + caster AP/100); x critPower only if the cast crit; x0.5 if that ally is enraged; Math.round.
effects.resolution: applied = rounded result added to that ally's shield, only if its hp > 0; stacks additively. Per-ally figures can differ (belt, enraged).

effects.mode: count.ult % 3 == 2 (2nd, 5th, ... cast; also the default branch)
effects.scaling: Per enemy: handleSpecialDamage with apBoost default true: x (1 + AP/100); x critPower (reduced by Rocky Helmet / Black Augurite on the target) only if the cast crit (canCritByDefault false, needs ABILITY_CRIT); other multipliers as in sibling single-target records.
effects.resolution: the figure handed to PokemonState.handleDamage per enemy (an intermediate input, not guaranteed final HP damage) is divided by (1 + ARMOR_FACTOR x speDef), rounded up with a minimum of 1, and the enemy's shield absorbs first; takenDamage = shield damage + HP damage (HP part capped at current hp); 0 for an enemy with protect / skydiving / magicBounce. Each enemy resolves separately.

buffs: mode 0 (every third cast, the 3rd first): team speed +10/20/40 (requested, raw)
shields: mode 1 (the 1st cast and every third after): team shield 10/20/40 (requested, raw)

starBehavior.note: All three tables are indexed by the caster's stars; the 4-star column (80, also the ?? fallback) is not reachable by the bare factory star counts of these units.

DRUM_BEATING.repeatedCastsAndModes: Stateful through pokemon.count.ult, incremented by the base process on every cast of any ability handler that calls super.process. Starting at 0, casts go shield (ult=1), damage (ult=2), speed (ult=3), shield (4) ... count.ult starts at 0: the Count class declares `ult = 0` (count.ts:6), PokemonEntity's constructor builds `new Count()` (pokemon-entity.ts:167) and Simulation.addPokemon constructs a fresh PokemonEntity for each unit placed in a fight (simulation.ts:346), so the first cast is the shield mode. The only reset of count.ult in pokemon-entity.ts is the VOLT_SURGE branch of resurrect() (lines 1552-1554), not DRUM_BEATING.
DRUM_BEATING.rawVsResolved: Requested: 10/20/40 per mode for 1/2/3 stars. Speed applied = requested x belt x (1 + AP/100) x crit, clamped to 300 (a Melmetal-passive ally gets half of the belted value as an Attack gain, rounded and belted a second time, and no speed). Shield applied = requested x belt, x (1 + AP/100), x crit, x0.5 if enraged, rounded. Damage applied = requested x (1 + AP/100) x crit etc., then an intermediate SPE_DEF division with a minimum of 1 and shield absorption (not guaranteed final HP damage). Final values depend on untraced item and field effects.

EXPANDING_FORCE.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
EXPANDING_FORCE.scope: The three units in appliesTo declare EXPANDING_FORCE: Blipbug (1 star), Dottler (2 stars), Orbeetle (3 stars), all range 1 and maxPP 85. Units not listed are not covered.
EXPANDING_FORCE.summary: First gives the caster a Psychic Field if it has none; if it already has one, gives one to the nearest ally (by Manhattan distance, ties in board-cell order) that lacks it, if any ally lacks it. Then, for EVERY ally of the caster's team that has a Psychic Field after that optional grant (caster included, and including allies that already held a field before this unit's first cast), deals SPECIAL damage (requested 10/20/40 by stars) to every enemy in the 8 cells around that ally, with the caster as attacker. An enemy adjacent to several field allies is hit once per such ally (overlapping hits are kept). The caster holds the field after the first step, so its damage also gets the attacker-has-Psychic-Field x1.2 inside handleDamage. Pinned-strategy probe: a caster without a field plus one already-field-bearing ally -> the first cast emits around both, not just the caster.

targeting.who: field grant: the caster, or the nearest field-less ally; damage: every enemy standing in a cell adjacent to any ally that has a Psychic Field
targeting.note: requiresTarget is false: the strategy does not use a cast target. Which fights make it cast (PP gain, silence) is generic and was not read.

geometry.shape: the 8 cells around each Psychic-Field ally (Board.getAdjacentCells, centre excluded), clipped to the board; one hit per (field ally, adjacent enemy) pair

effects.target: the caster if it has none, otherwise the nearest ally without one
effects.scaling: No numbers. Status.addPsychicField sets the flag only if not already set; a SURGE_SURFER-passive unit that gains the field also makes a raw addSpeed(30, itself, 0, false) request (no AP, no crit; it goes through the addSpeed helper, with Big Eater Belt, Twist Band, the Melmetal branch and the 0..300 clamp), so +30 is a request, not a guaranteed final speed change. Nearest = lowest Manhattan distance to the caster, ties in board-cell order.
effects.resolution: At most one new unit gets the field per cast, and none when every ally already has it (no eligible ally may remain), so the number of damage sources does not necessarily grow by one per cast. The field has no timer in this code; it is removed by clearAllStatus or when a PSYCHIC_TERRAIN-passive unit dies (other callers of those paths not traced).

declaredRaw.description: no numbers: sets the Psychic Field flag on the caster, or on the nearest ally without one

effects.target: every enemy adjacent to each Psychic-Field ally, once per such ally
effects.scaling: requested = table[stars-1] per hit. handleSpecialDamage with default apBoost true: x (1 + AP/100) of the caster; x critPower (reduced by Rocky Helmet / Black Augurite on the target) only if the cast crit (canCritByDefault false, so needs ABILITY_CRIT). In handleDamage the attacker (caster) with a Psychic Field adds x1.2 and an enraged caster x2.

EXPANDING_FORCE.positionalConditions: Damage position depends on where the Psychic-Field allies stand; the caster's own position matters only for who is nearest when spreading the field.
EXPANDING_FORCE.repeatedCastsAndModes: Stateful through the field flags. Each cast first grants the field: to the caster if it lacks one, otherwise to the nearest field-less ally if any ally lacks it (none may remain, then nothing is granted). Then EVERY currently field-bearing ally radiates the damage, including allies that already had the field from other sources before this unit's first cast. The number of damage sources therefore grows by at most one per cast and not at all when no eligible ally remains; overlapping hits on one enemy are kept.
EXPANDING_FORCE.rawVsResolved: Requested: damage 10/20/40 per hit for 1/2/3 stars. Applied per hit = requested x (1 + AP/100) x optional crit multiplier, x1.2 if the caster has a Psychic Field (normally yes), x2 if the caster is enraged, then an intermediate SPE_DEF division with a minimum of 1 (not guaranteed final HP damage); takenDamage includes shield damage. Number of hits per enemy = number of field allies adjacent to it. Final values depend on untraced item and field effects.

unresolved: Other sources of Psychic Field (the item effect at items.ts around line 917, terrain passives, TERRAIN_PULSE, MIST/PSYCHIC terrain synergies) change which allies already hold the field and were not traced; fields granted by them also count as damage sources here
Callers of clearAllStatus (which removes the field) were not traced
Sort ties and the order of enemy hits follow board.cells order; JavaScript sort stability was assumed from the language definition, not run

RAGING_BULL.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
RAGING_BULL.scope: The four units in appliesTo (Tauros and its three breeds) declare RAGING_BULL in this production reference, all 3 stars, maxPP 100, range 1, passive NONE in the catalog. Each breed is its own registered class; the strategy is shared.
RAGING_BULL.summary: Single-target ability. As written, the strategy (1) calls target.status.triggerArmorReduction(3000, pokemon) with the CASTER as the entity argument, (2) sets the target's reflect, protect and magicBounce flags to false and their cooldowns to 0 directly, and (3) requests SPECIAL damage (20/40/80/160 raw by the caster's stars). Rune Protect is checked on the target's status inside triggerArmorReduction and refuses only a NEW application; the direct flag clearing in (2) still happens. That refusal does not make the target's current armorReduction flag false: the damage step reads the flag as it is when the hit is processed (halved SPE_DEF if it is true, from this application or an earlier one still flagged; the normal SPE_DEF if no flag is set). The damage request in (3) is made whether or not the application was accepted. Duration reductions (Swift Swim, Hydration, Water Veil / Surge Surfer, Odd Keystone) read the entity that was supplied, i.e. the caster, not the target. Protect and magicBounce are cleared before the damage call, so they do not block it; skydiving is not cleared and still blocks it.

targeting.who: the cast target passed to the strategy (the caster's current target)
targeting.note: requiresTarget is the base default true; how the target is chosen before the cast was not traced beyond the attacking-state gate.

effects.scaling: AP: damage x (1 + AP/100) (apBoost defaults to true); the cast's crit flag multiplies by critPower (reduced by the target's critReductionFactor) only if the cast crit, which requires EffectEnum.ABILITY_CRIT because canCritByDefault is false
effects.resolution: requested amount = raw x AP factor [x crit]. handleDamage uses Math.round(speDef / 2) whenever the target's current armorReduction flag is true when the hit is processed (a successful application sets it just before; a Rune-Protect-refused application leaves the flag unchanged, so with no earlier flag the full SPE_DEF is used). The division is an intermediate calculation (ceil, min 1) and later untraced modifiers follow, so it is not the final HP loss; takenDamage (not used by this strategy) would count HP removed plus shield damage. Blocked entirely only by skydiving (protect and magicBounce were cleared first).

declaredRaw.description: reflect, protect and magicBounce flags set to false and their cooldowns to 0 (six unconditional assignments)

effects.scaling: none
effects.resolution: after armor reduction, before the damage call; none: the six assignments run unconditionally, including when the target has Rune Protect (which only blocks the armor reduction); skydiving is not touched. protect: handleDamage and handleSpecialDamage no longer block; magicBounce: the bounce branch in handleSpecialDamage no longer fires; reflect: only affects PHYSICAL damage in handleDamage and this hit is SPECIAL. Protect can be reapplied by triggerProtect later (unless the target is enraged); the removal is not a lasting immunity.

statusEffects.scaling: none from AP or crit
statusEffects.applicationOrder: first, before the barrier flags are cleared and before the damage
statusEffects.guards: a NEW application is refused if the TARGET's status has runeProtect (checked on `this` in triggerArmorReduction); the refusal neither sets nor clears the flag and does not cancel the damage. A refused application (Rune Protect) does not prove the target's CURRENT armorReduction flag is false: the damage step reads the flag as it is when the hit is processed. triggerRuneProtect calls clearNegativeStatus, which zeroes armorReductionCooldown but not the boolean, so a flag set before Rune Protect appeared stays true until updateArmorReduction runs; with no earlier flag, a refused application leaves the normal defenses in place. When applied, the duration goes through applyStatusDurationReductions(duration, pkm) where pkm is the entity argument the strategy supplied, the CASTER: if the caster has SWIFT_SWIM the duration is x0.7, else HYDRATION x0.5, else WATER_VEIL / SURGE_SURFER x0.3 (all Math.round), and each Odd Keystone in the CASTER's player's items takes a further 10 % off (Math.round). So a caster with HYDRATION turns 3000 into 1500, whereas HYDRATION on the target alone changes nothing. A new application replaces the remaining time only if longer. Pinned-helper probe: plain 3000, caster HYDRATION 1500, HYDRATION on the target only 3000, caster with 2 Odd Keystones 2400, target Rune Protect: no armor reduction
statusEffects.combatEffect: while set, handleDamage uses Math.round(def / 2) and Math.round(speDef / 2) for the damage division; the same halving appears in the POWER_LENS retaliation computation (handleSpecialDamage) and in an items.ts second-hit calculation. Other readers of the flag were not searched beyond app/core and app/models. The code is described as written; whether passing the caster is intended is not asserted.

starBehavior.note: indexed by the casting entity's stars; all four listed units are 3-star in the catalog, so their bare value is 80. The 160 value (also the fallback) is not reachable by their bare star count. The 3000 ms armor reduction does not vary with stars.

ZAP_CANNON.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
ZAP_CANNON.scope: The four units in appliesTo declare ZAP_CANNON in this production reference (all maxPP 100, range 3). Charjabug and Grubbin declare passive HATCH, Deoxys Attack declares ALIEN_DNA and Vikavolt declares none; those passives were not traced here. The strategy is shared; differences are star count and stats.
ZAP_CANNON.summary: Single-target: the strategy calls triggerArmorReduction(duration, target) and then triggerParalysis(duration, target, caster) with the same raw duration (1000/2000/4000/8000 ms by stars), then unconditionally requests SPECIAL damage (raw 25/50/100/200 by stars, apBoost true). Both statuses are applied only if the target's status has no Rune Protect (paralysis also needs no IMMUNITY_PARALYSIS); Rune Protect does not stop the damage request. Rune Protect refuses only a NEW armor-reduction application and does not make the target's current armorReduction flag false: the damage step reads the flag as it is when the hit is processed (halved SPE_DEF if it is true, from this application or an earlier one still flagged; the normal SPE_DEF if no flag is set), so the halved-SPE_DEF effect is conditional on that flag. Each timer keeps the larger of its existing remaining duration and the new request after the target's duration reductions. The crit flag is the cast's crit, rolled only with ABILITY_CRIT.

targeting.who: the cast target passed to the strategy (the caster's current target)
targeting.note: requiresTarget is the base default true; how the target is chosen before the cast was not traced beyond the attacking-state gate.

effects.scaling: requested amount = raw table value. handleSpecialDamage applies AP: damage x (1 + AP/100) (apBoost passed as true); the cast's crit flag multiplies by 1 + (critPower - 1) x critReductionFactor (0 with a Rocky Helmet on the target, minus 0.1 per Black Augurite of its player, not below 0).
effects.resolution: the damage request is made after the two status calls and does not depend on them. handleDamage then computes an intermediate value damage / (1 + 0.05 x SPE_DEF), where SPE_DEF is Math.round(speDef / 2) whenever the target's current armorReduction flag is true when the hit is processed (a successful application sets it just before; a Rune-Protect-refused application leaves the flag unchanged), rounds up with a minimum of 1 and applies other modifiers and shields not traced in full; this is not guaranteed final HP damage. Blocked (takenDamage 0) by protect / skydiving / magicBounce; those do not stop the two statuses, which are applied before the damage call. takenDamage includes shield damage; the return value is unused. Pinned-helper probe (1 star, AP 0, no crit): with Rune Protect on the target there is no armor reduction and no paralysis, but a request of 25 SPECIAL (apBoost true) still occurs.

statusEffects.scaling: none from AP or crit (the strategy passes the raw duration)
statusEffects.applicationOrder: first, before the paralysis and the damage
statusEffects.guards: a NEW application is refused if the target's status has runeProtect (checked on the status the method is called on; the refusal neither sets nor clears the flag and does not cancel the damage request). A refused application (Rune Protect) does not prove the target's CURRENT armorReduction flag is false: the damage step reads the flag as it is when the hit is processed. triggerRuneProtect calls clearNegativeStatus, which zeroes armorReductionCooldown but not the boolean, so a flag set before Rune Protect appeared stays true until updateArmorReduction runs; with no earlier flag, a refused application leaves the normal defenses in place. Otherwise the strategy supplies the TARGET as the entity argument, so the duration reductions read the target (SWIFT_SWIM x0.7, else HYDRATION x0.5, else WATER_VEIL / SURGE_SURFER x0.3, then -10 % per ODD_KEYSTONE of the target's player, rounded). Timer rule: `if (duration > armorReductionCooldown) armorReductionCooldown = round(duration)`, so the timer keeps the larger of the existing remaining time and the new reduced request (probe: a 1000 ms request against 5000 ms remaining leaves 5000; against 400 ms remaining it sets 1000; target HYDRATION turns 1000 into 500).
statusEffects.combatEffect: while armorReduction is set, DEF and SPE_DEF are halved (Math.round(value / 2)) when handleDamage resolves damage on the target; the Power Lens retaliation computation in handleSpecialDamage also halves SPE_DEF. Other users of status.armorReduction (items.ts:165) were seen but not read.

statusEffects.scaling: none from AP or crit: the strategy leaves apBoost at its default false, so triggerParalysis does not multiply by (1 + AP/100)
statusEffects.applicationOrder: second, after armor reduction and before the damage
statusEffects.guards: not applied with runeProtect or IMMUNITY_PARALYSIS (probe: IMMUNITY_PARALYSIS alone blocks only the paralysis); STORM weather multiplies the duration by 1.3, then by (1 - 0.2 x ELECTRIC_QUARTZ count of the target's player) if any; then the target's applyStatusDurationReductions as above. Timer rule: `if (duration > paralysisCooldown) paralysisCooldown = round(duration)`, the larger of the existing remaining time and the new reduced request. A CHERI_BERRY holder eats the berry after a successful application (it heals the paralysis and grants IMMUNITY_PARALYSIS).
statusEffects.combatEffect: a paralysed unit uses half speed for its attack cooldown (attacking-state) and its movement speed (move-speed), and cannot dodge basic attacks (handleAttack dodge check). Other uses of status.paralysis (bug-buzz, force-palm, zing-zap, synergies.ts, passives.ts) were seen but not read.

EXPLOSION.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
EXPLOSION.scope: The four units in appliesTo declare EXPLOSION in this production reference. The strategy is a shared constant instance (explosionStrategy); differences between the units are star count, stats and maxPP.

dispatch.registry: AbilityStrategies[Ability.EXPLOSION] = explosionStrategy (the constant `export const explosionStrategy = new ExplosionStrategy()` in explosion.ts)

EXPLOSION.summary: Area self-centred special damage: every unit of the other team standing in the 8 cells around the caster takes SPECIAL damage (raw 50/100/200/400 by caster stars), and the caster then damages itself with the same raw amount unless it holds Protective Pads. If the caster has Magic Bounce active, that self hit is not applied immediately: handleSpecialDamage returns takenDamage 0 and queues a delayed callback (see the self-damage effect; its crit is the incoming crit OR a fresh ABILITY_CRIT roll when it runs). An enemy with Magic Bounce likewise queues a bounce aimed at the caster.

targeting.who: enemy units in the cells adjacent to the caster (not adjacent to the cast target)
targeting.note: requiresTarget is the base default true, so the caster still needs a target in range to cast; the target parameter is only used by super.process for the animation and is not used for the damage. How the target is picked before the cast was not read.

geometry.shape: the 8 board cells around the caster (3x3 minus centre), clipped to the board; allies and empty cells are skipped

effects.target: each enemy in the adjacent cells
effects.scaling: AP: damage x (1 + AP/100) (apBoost defaults to true); the crit flag multiplies by critPower (reduced by the target's crit reduction) only if the cast rolled a crit (needs ABILITY_CRIT because canCritByDefault is false)
effects.resolution: requested = the raw amount; after handleSpecialDamage AP/crit scaling the target's SPE_DEF division (damage / (1 + 0.05 x SPE_DEF), ceil, min 1) and later untraced modifiers; a target with protect / skydiving / magicBounce takes none (takenDamage 0). Damage lands on a shield first (whole amount unless flinched); a Protective Pads holder doubles the amount that hits a shield. The strategy does not read takenDamage, so applied damage does not feed back into the ability. A target with magicBounce also queues a 500-delayed SPECIAL bounce request aimed at the caster unless the caster holds Protective Pads (the bounce amount was not traced further).

BLAZE_KICK.summary: Burns the cast target for a base 2000 ms, deals SPECIAL damage (raw 30/60/120/240 by stars, x1.3 if the target was already burning before the cast), then requests a forced displacement of the target to the last empty cell visited by effectInOrientation along the 8-way direction from the caster toward the target. As written, the RIGHT direction loops `x < board.rows` (6) although the production board has 8 columns and 6 rows, so columns 6 and 7 are never visited going RIGHT; if no empty cell is visited, no move is requested and the target stays (the damage and burn happen regardless).

The RIGHT case uses `x < board.rows`; on the 8-column x 6-row production board (simulation.ts:104, config/game/board.ts) that excludes columns 6 and 7. The final fallback of effectInOrientation (board.ts:913-917) calls the effect once on the target's own cell when no enemy was visited; that cell is occupied, so BLAZE_KICK's callback ignores it and it does not provide a free destination. AQUA_STEP.scope: The three units in appliesTo declare AQUA_STEP: Quaxly (1 star), Quaxwell (2 stars) and Quaquaval (3 stars); all have range 1 and maxPP 100 and no passive. The strategy is shared; unit differences are the star count (table index).
AQUA_STEP.summary: The strategy computes a reference coordinate one sign-step from the caster toward the cast target (caster.x + sign(dx), caster.y + sign(dy)), asks board.getClosestAvailablePlace for the free cell closest (Manhattan) to that reference anywhere on the board, and requests a non-forced moveTo there. Because the search covers ALL free cells, the movement is not limited to one cell: it is the free cell nearest the reference, which can be far away on a crowded board (probe: caster (0,0), target (1,0), only free cell (7,5) -> move requested to (7,5)). With no free cell no move is requested. In every case a DelayedCommand with nominal delay 300 is queued; when it runs it requests SPECIAL damage on the cast target (raw 25/50/100/200 by stars) and adds speed to the caster (raw 10/15/20/25 by stars; AP-scaled). The 300 is a nominal delay consumed by update(dt) (the command runs on the first update that takes the delay below 0), not a guaranteed execution time.

targeting.who: the cast target (damage); caster itself (step and speed gain)
targeting.note: The reference coordinate uses the cast target's position at cast time; the delayed damage uses the target entity (its position is read again for the broadcast only). The damage and speed command is queued whether or not a destination cell was found.

geometry.shape: destination = the free cell closest (Manhattan) to (caster.x + sign(dx), caster.y + sign(dy)) among ALL free cells of the board (not limited to one cell); single-target damage afterwards

effects.scaling: requested = table value. applied by handleSpecialDamage: damage x (1 + AP/100) (apBoost true by default); x critPower (adjusted by target items) if the cast crit.
effects.resolution: after the delay, PokemonState.handleDamage computes an intermediate value damage / (1 + ARMOR_FACTOR x SPE_DEF), rounded up with a minimum of 1, and the shield absorbs before HP; this is not guaranteed final HP damage. protect / skydiving / magicBounce on the target at the time the command fires block the hit entirely. takenDamage includes shield damage. The command is queued even when no destination cell exists. Probe: the queued command has delay 300, has not run after update(300) and has run after a further update(1) (damage 25 SPECIAL requested, speed gain 10 with apBoost 1); this shows the delay is consumed by update(dt), not that 300 is a guaranteed timing.

POWDER.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
POWDER.scope: The 22 units in appliesTo declare POWDER in this production reference: Scatterbug (1 star), Spewpa (2 stars) and the 20 Vivillon forms (3 stars each). The strategy is shared; unit differences are only the star count (table index), range 2, passive (Scatterbug HATCH, Spewpa SPEWPA, per the catalog) and stats. Those two passives are NOT investigated here.
POWDER.summary: Picks the enemy with the highest current SPEED among enemies within the caster's range (the cast target if none is in range), then for every cell on the straight (supercover) line from the caster to that enemy, each enemy standing on the line takes special damage and has its SPEED lowered; the SPEED is given back after 5000 ms. Allies on the line are untouched. The speed change is a REQUEST: addSpeed passes the value through the holder's item helpers and the 0..300 clamp, so the applied change and the later restoration can differ from the requested amount (Twist Band flips the enemy debuff into a gain, Big Eater Belt scales only the positive restoration, a MELMETAL victim changes Attack instead). Pinned-helper probe: victim speed 100, requested nerf 30 -> plain 70 then 100; Big Eater Belt 70 then 107; Twist Band 130 then 160.

targeting.who: the enemy with the highest speed in range (range from the caster's own stat, Chebyshev distance, centre excluded; no targettable/visibility filter is applied in this function); ties keep the stable sort order of the board scan. The effect then hits EVERY enemy on the line to that enemy, not only that enemy.
targeting.note: The line is a supercover line from caster to the chosen enemy, so it can include enemies nearer than the fastest one (and diagonals can touch extra cells). If no enemy is in range the cast target is used instead. The sort uses current speed (after buffs/debuffs at cast time). Enemy scan order within Board.getCellsInRange is row-major (y outer, x inner); the effect of ties on that was derived from the loop, not executed.

geometry.shape: line from caster to the fastest in-range enemy (supercover, inclusive of both end cells); only enemy occupants are affected; the range only limits the choice of the fastest enemy, not the line cells

effects.scaling: AP: damage x (1 + AP/100) (apBoost defaults to true); the cast's crit flag multiplies by critPower only if the cast crit (needs ABILITY_CRIT: canCritByDefault is false)
effects.resolution: then the target's SPE_DEF division (damage / (1 + 0.05 x SPE_DEF), ceil, min 1) and later untraced modifiers; blocked entirely by protect / skydiving / magicBounce. Damage is applied once per enemy on the line.

effects.scaling: nerf = min(victim's current speed, rawFactor x (1 + AP/100) x (crit ? critPower : 1)); crit uses the cast's crit flag (needs ABILITY_CRIT). addSpeed is then called with apBoost 0 and crit false, so no second AP scaling there. The request is capped at the victim's CURRENT speed (it is a plain min, not rounded).
effects.resolution: applied change per holder item (addSpeed lines 752-780; probe: 3 stars, AP 0, victim speed 100, requested nerf 30): plain 100 -> 70 -> 100. Big Eater Belt does NOT scale the enemy debuff (a negative value from another team) but scales the positive restoration x1.25 rounded down (30 -> 37): 70 -> 107. Twist Band flips the enemy debuff into a speed GAIN (100 -> 130) and the restoration adds the amount again (-> 160), so the holder gains speed twice; results clamp to 0..MAX_SPEED (290 -> 300 -> 300). The nerf is capped at the victim's current speed (20 -> 0 -> 20). MELMETAL victim: no speed change; addSpeed runs the item helpers, then addAttack(value x 0.5) which rounds and runs the helpers a second time (Attack 40 -> 25 -> 40; with a Belt the restoration is belted twice, +23, -> 48), with an Attack floor of 1. The restoration is a separate +amount queued on the victim after a nominal 5000 ms (the command runs on the first update after the delay goes below 0); it re-adds the REQUESTED amount through the helpers, not the previous speed, and other speed changes in between stay. BITE.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
BITE.scope: The five units in appliesTo declare BITE in this production reference (all with passive NONE in the catalog). The strategy is shared; differences are star count and stats.
BITE.summary: Single-target special damage (40/80/120 raw by stars); the caster then requests a heal of ceil(30 %) of the takenDamage value returned by that damage call, and flinches the cast target for 5000 ms if that value is above 0. takenDamage is a component accounting with named exceptions (see the damage resolution), not the pre-defence amount and not universally the HP actually lost: the Cover Band cover ally's result, the Shiny Charm zeroing and the Fossil extra accounting all feed the heal and the flinch. The heal request then passes handleHeal: a wounded caster receives no HP heal, but the shared Blood Moon / Blood Stone branch can still request a compensating shield.

targeting.note: requiresTarget is the base default true; how the target is chosen before the cast was not read.

effects.scaling: AP: damage x (1 + AP/100) (apBoost defaults to true); the cast's crit flag multiplies by critPower (reduced by the target's critReductionFactor) only if the cast crit (needs ABILITY_CRIT: canCritByDefault is false)
effects.resolution: intermediate, not guaranteed final HP damage: handleDamage divides by (1 + 0.05 x SPE_DEF) (ceil, min 1) among other steps. The returned takenDamage: ordinary accounting is the part absorbed by the shield (with flinch both the shield part and the residual are ceil(0.5 x reduced); Protective Pads on the attacker double the shield part before it is capped at the shield, the excess moving to the residual) plus min(residual, current HP), rounded. It is NOT universally 'HP lost plus shield loss': it is 0 for a dead or resurrecting, protected or skydiving target (handleSpecialDamage also returns 0 for magicBounce); the Shiny Charm branch zeroes it and consumes the charm; the Fossil branch adds min(0.5 x shield, residual) on top, so it can exceed the incoming damage (probe: incoming 300 returns 500 while the target's HP stays unchanged); a Cover Band redirect returns the cover ally's own result, while the original target keeps its HP and has already lost the shield part. Blocked entirely by protect / skydiving / magicBounce (takenDamage 0, so no heal and no flinch). Pinned-helper probe (SPECIAL 100, HP 500): plain 100; shield 40 -> 40 + 60 = 100; shield 200 -> 100 on the shield; shield 200 with flinch -> 50 + 50; overkill capped at HP 40; Protective Pads shield 30 -> 200; Fossil branch 300 -> 500; Cover Band redirect -> the cover ally's 100.

effects.resolution: handleHeal then applies: a wounded caster (status.wound) receives no HP heal (healReceived 0), but when the weather is BLOODMOON and the caster's player holds BLOOD_STONE the same call first requests a shield of round(0.3 x stones x heal) through addShield (pokemon-state.ts:315-331); nothing for a caster at 0 hp or protected; x1.3 BUFF_HEAL_RECEIVED, x0.5 burn, x0.5 enraged, x1.2 ZENITH weather; rounded and capped at missing HP; overheal on a GRASS-synergy unit adds max HP. Probe (raw 40, caster 500/1000): heal 12 (HP 512); wounded: HP 500, with Blood Moon + one Blood Stone a shield of 4.

statusEffects.combatEffect: while flinched and while the target's shield is above 0, handleDamage splits the reduced damage with ceil operations: damageOnShield = ceil(0.5 x reduced) and residual = ceil(0.5 x reduced), so an odd amount puts one more in total than reduced (5 -> 3 + 3). TELEPORT.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
TELEPORT.scope: The six units in appliesTo declare TELEPORT in this production reference. Passives of Mew (SYNCHRO), Cosmog (COSMOG) and Cosmoem (COSMOEM) are not investigated here.
TELEPORT.summary: Relocates the caster to a free cell chosen by Board.getFlyAwayCell and, if a cell was found, marks the caster with TELEPORT_NEXT_ATTACK. The next execution of PokemonState.attack on a living target consumes the mark whatever happens to that basic attack: the bonus special damage (15/30/60/120 raw by stars, AP-scaled, rounded up) is added to the attack's special part and the mark deleted before any damage call, so a DODGED attack (basic damage 0) still requests the bonus, a protected or skydiving target blocks the bonus request, and a Magic Bounce target blocks it and can queue a delayed reflection at the caster, which a Protective Pads holder suppresses. The cast itself deals no damage. While the mark is set the caster cannot cast (canCast is false), and if the unit never attacks the mark simply stays set.

targeting.who: none at cast time (requiresTarget false: castable without walking up to a target). The destination cell is chosen by getFlyAwayCell from enemies/cells on the board.
targeting.note: getFlyAwayCell: returns null if no living enemy exists. Otherwise from unoccupied cells it keeps those strictly beyond the caster's own range from its current cell, and of those only cells within the caster's range of at least one targettable enemy; among them it keeps the lowest 'enemy threat count' (living enemies whose own range reaches the cell), then the highest distanceM from the caster's current position, then picks one at random. If no cell qualifies it falls back to getSafePlaceAwayFrom (origin = the caster's current target position or its own position, max distance = its range) plus the closest enemy; if that fails it returns null and the caster neither moves nor gets the mark. The random pick makes the destination non-deterministic. distanceC/distanceM metrics and getSafePlaceAwayFrom internals were not read.

geometry.shape: caster relocation to one free cell (swapCells); no area effect

effects.scaling: added to the caster's next basic attack as specialDamage: ceil(raw x (1 + AP/100) x (abilityCrit ? 1 + (critPower - 1) x critReductionFactor : 1)) where abilityCrit = the caster has ABILITY_CRIT AND that BASIC attack's own crit roll succeeded (the cast passes crit false to super.process). It is handed to handleSpecialDamage with crit false and apBoost false, so AP and crit are not applied twice. The array has no fallback for stars above 4 (unit-star index only).
effects.resolution: the mark is checked and deleted at pokemon-state.ts:163-174, after the dodge roll (100-112) and the protect / skydiving test (114-117) have only zeroed the basic damage and cleared isAttackSuccessful, and before the damage calls (244-282); it lives inside the branch that requires the target to be alive. The bonus is then requested through handleSpecialDamage (257-269): blocked (takenDamage 0) when the target has protect or skydiving; with Magic Bounce it is blocked and a delayed reflection at the attacker is queued, unless the attacker holds Protective Pads, which suppress it; the target's SPE_DEF division and shields are the intermediate steps of handleDamage and not guaranteed final HP damage. Pinned-helper probe (1 star, ATK 30, AP 0, target HP 500): normal hit 455 (30 physical + 15 bonus); dodged 485 (bonus lands, dodgeCount 1); protected target 500; Magic Bounce target 470 (physical lands, bonus blocked, bounce queued); crit roll with ABILITY_CRIT 410 (bonus 30), without it 425; every case consumes the mark. A marked unit that never attacks keeps the mark, and canCast stays false (pokemon-entity.ts:250-256).

starBehavior.note: damage is indexed by the casting entity's stars at the time of the attack ([15,30,60,120][stars-1]); the cast does not scale with stars otherwise. maxPP is 50 for Abra/Kadabra/Alakazam/Mew and 100 for Cosmog/Cosmoem.

Requested bonus = ceil(raw x (1 + AP/100) [x crit factor when ABILITY_CRIT and the attack's own crit roll succeeded]); it is consumed by the first attack on a living target (dodged, protected or not) and is delivered or blocked by handleSpecialDamage as described; target-side SPE_DEF division and shields are intermediate steps, not guaranteed final HP damage.
