SUCTION_HEAL.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
SUCTION_HEAL.scope: The three units in appliesTo declare SUCTION_HEAL: Tynamo (1 star), Eelektrik (2 stars), Eelektross (3 stars); all range 1, maxPP 80, no passive. The strategy is shared; unit differences are the star count (table index). Units sharing the identifier but not listed are not covered.
SUCTION_HEAL.summary: Needs a target. The caster spends its PP, then every occupied cell of a forward cone (range 2, aimed at the target) that holds an enemy takes special damage of raw 15/30/60/120 (by caster stars; AP-scaled; crit possible via the passed crit flag), and for each such hit the caster requests a heal of 0.5 x the takenDamage that handleSpecialDamage returns (apBoost 0, no crit, so AP and crit do not scale it). takenDamage is the returned figure, not the HP actually lost: it includes the part absorbed by the target's shield (flinch splits the reduced hit 50/50 and Protective Pads on the caster double the shield part), the HP part is capped at the target's current HP, it is 0 for a protected / skydiving / magic-bouncing, dead or resurrecting target and when Shiny Charm triggers, the Fossil synergy branch can add shield damage so it exceeds the HP lost, and a Cover Band holder that takes the hit makes the returned value the cover ally's. The request then goes through PokemonState.handleHeal: a wounded caster receives no HP (with BLOODMOON weather and a Blood Stone owned by its player the same call first requests addShield(round(0.3 x stones x the requested heal)), which Big Eater Belt can raise); an unwounded caster with status.protect receives nothing (Rune Protect does not matter; a wounded one has already taken the wound branch, so Protect does not stop the Blood Stone shield); otherwise BUFF_HEAL_RECEIVED x1.3, burn x0.5, enraged x0.5 and ZENITH x1.2 apply, the result is rounded and capped at the caster's missing HP, and on a caster with the GRASS synergy effect the overheal requests addMaxHP(0.4 x overheal), which also raises current HP. One heal per enemy hit, so several enemies in the cone give several heals. No heal and no damage when no enemy stands in the cone (PP is still spent).

targeting.who: enemies (cell.value.team differs from the caster's team) standing in the forward cone cells
targeting.note: The target is only used to orient the cone (getCellsInFront sets the caster's orientation toward it); the damaged units are whatever enemies stand in the cone cells, which need not include the target. Allies and empty cells are skipped.

geometry.shape: cone: the caster's orientation toward the target plus its two adjacent orientations, expanded for r = 1..2 (cells that coincide are de-duplicated; off-board cells dropped)

effects.target: each enemy in the cone cells
effects.scaling: requested = table value by the caster's stars. Applied through handleSpecialDamage with the default apBoost = true: x(1 + caster AP/100); DOUBLE_DAMAGE x2 and strange-steam x1.2 where present; x(1 + (critPower - 1) x reduction) when the crit flag is true (reduction 0 against Rocky Helmet, -0.1 per Black Augurite). No rounding before the defence step.
effects.resolution: requested (raw table) -> applied (after AP / crit factors, special type) -> PokemonState.handleDamage: SPE_DEF division, min-1 floor (see core-mechanics section A), shield first then HP -> takenDamage = shield damage + min(residual, current HP), rounded. Blocked (protect / skydiving / magicBounce) or dead targets report takenDamage 0. Known accounting exceptions that change the returned takenDamage relative to the HP lost: flinch splits the reduced hit 50/50 between shield and HP; an attacker's Protective Pads double the shield part; the Fossil synergy branch adds shield damage on top of the HP part (taken 500, HP unchanged for damage 300 on 500 HP in the probe); Shiny Charm zeroes takenDamage; a Cover Band ally that takes a lethal hit makes the result the cover ally's.

declaredRaw.of: takenDamage reported by handleSpecialDamage for that enemy

effects.scaling: requested = 0.5 x takenDamage of that hit (an applied-then-resolved damage figure, not the raw table value). handleHeal is called with apBoost 0 and crit false, so AP and crit do not scale the heal. Then PokemonState.handleHeal in this order: wound branch (see resolution), the guard hp > 0 && !status.protect, x1.3 BUFF_HEAL_RECEIVED, x0.5 burning, x0.5 enraged, x1.2 ZENITH weather; Math.round; capped by the caster's missing HP; the rounded excess over missing HP is the overheal (Grass branch below).
effects.resolution: requested (0.5 x takenDamage) -> applied (after the modifiers, rounded) -> healReceived (after the missing-HP cap; the rest is overheal). A wounded caster receives 0 HP, BUT with BLOODMOON weather and a Blood Stone held by the caster's player the wound branch first requests addShield(round(0.3 x stones x requested heal), caster, 0, false) (requested heal = 0.5 x takenDamage, before modifiers); that request goes through the entity addShield (Big Eater Belt x1.25 rounded down) and the state's addShield (needs hp > 0, enraged halves, rounded), so the final shield can differ from the request. The wound branch comes before the Protect test, so Protect does not stop that shield. An unwounded caster with status.protect receives 0 HP, no Grass overheal and no shield; status.runeProtect is not read by handleHeal. On a caster with the GRASS synergy effect the overheal (rounded modified heal minus missing HP, the part not applied) requests addMaxHP(0.4 x overheal, caster, 0, false, false); addMaxHP rounds, applies Big Eater Belt / Twist Band, raises maxHP and also current HP by the final value, and the amount is not added to healDone. Requested, applied and final amounts differ for each of these indirect branches. Shield damage dealt counts in takenDamage and therefore in the heal. A Shiny Charm trigger on the victim makes takenDamage 0 and so no heal. One heal per enemy hit, so several enemies in the cone give several heals.

starBehavior.note: indexed by the casting entity's stars (stars - 1); 120 is not reached at the factory star counts of these units. Whether other mechanics change an entity's star count was not examined.

SUCTION_HEAL.positionalConditions: The cone is aimed at the target; only enemies inside the cone cells (distance up to 2 in the three forward orientations) are damaged and heal the caster. If no enemy stands in those cells nothing is damaged and no heal happens (PP is still spent).
SUCTION_HEAL.repeatedCastsAndModes: No stored state or modes; every cast recomputes the cone from the current board. getCellsInFront also overwrites the caster's orientation.
SUCTION_HEAL.rawVsResolved: Declared raw: damage 15/30/60 for 1/2/3 stars. Requested damage = raw; applied damage = raw x (1 + AP/100) x crit factor etc.; takenDamage = what handleDamage reports (after SPE_DEF, the min-1 floor, shield and HP cap, rounded). The heal requested is 0.5 x takenDamage (the returned figure, including shield damage and the exceptions above, not the HP lost); applied after heal modifiers and rounding (no AP, no crit); received after the missing-HP cap. Wound, Blood Moon + Blood Stone (addShield request, final after Big Eater Belt), status.protect (nothing at all) and Grass (addMaxHP(0.4 x overheal) request, final after the item helpers, also raises HP) are separate branches of handleHeal described in effects[1]; they are shared-helper rules (core-mechanics.md section J).
dependsOnUnverifiedGenericCombat: When the cast fires in a real fight (PP gain, silence, target acquisition) - only the abilities base class (PP spend, flags) was read
Crit resolution - only the crit parameter passed into handleSpecialDamage was read, not how the cast decides crit
Board.orientation (called by getCellsInFront) was not read, so the exact orientation chosen toward a given target is not stated
unresolved: Cone cell membership for a given caster/target geometry was not enumerated: only the construction in getCellsInFront was read (three orientations grown for 2 steps, de-duplicated)

Whether the target itself always stands inside the cone: the cone is built from the orientation toward the target, but the target's distance and the orientation rounding in Board.orientation were not checked
Ordering of the heals relative to the damage when several enemies are hit follows cells iteration order (a Set of coordinates in insertion order); not verified beyond reading

PARABOLIC_CHARGE.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
PARABOLIC_CHARGE.scope: The two units in appliesTo (Helioptile 1 star, Heliolisk 2 stars) declare PARABOLIC_CHARGE and both carry the passive DRY_SKIN in the catalog. Shared strategy. DRY_SKIN is a separate weather-driven periodic effect (see unresolved) and is not part of this ability.
PARABOLIC_CHARGE.summary: Heals the caster, then deals SPECIAL damage to the cast target. Heal request: 25 (1 star) / 50 (2 stars) raw (75 / 100 at 3 / 4+ stars: declared in the table but unused by the two bound baseline classes, Helioptile 1 star and Heliolisk 2 stars), with no AP or crit scaling. Damage raw: 25 (1 star) / 50 (2 stars) (100 / 200 at 3 / 4+) PLUS overHeal, where overHeal = max(0, requestedHeal + caster.hp - caster.maxHP) is computed BEFORE the heal from the caster's current HP and the UNMODIFIED requested heal. It therefore measures how much of the requested heal would exceed missing HP; it is not the overheal that handleHeal reports after its modifiers. The heal is requested first, the damage second, in the same call; the damage reads the overHeal value computed earlier, not the caster's HP after healing. Illustration only (arithmetic, not a fight): Heliolisk (heal 50) at 90/100 HP: pre-heal overHeal 40, damage raw 50 + 40 = 90 before AP and the target's speDef; with no heal modifiers handleHeal's own overheal is also 40 (healed 10), so a Grass Heliolisk would request addMaxHP(16) - but with, say, burning (x0.5) handleHeal would heal 25 capped to 10 and report overheal 15 while the damage still uses 40. AROMATHERAPY.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
AROMATHERAPY.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare AROMATHERAPY: Petilil (1 star) and Lilligant (2 stars); both have maxPP 100, range 1 and no declared passive. The strategy is shared; the only unit difference is the star count (table index).

dispatch.note: The strategy does not override requiresTarget or canCritByDefault, so the base defaults (target required, no crit unless the caster has ability crit) apply. The target passed to process is not used.

AROMATHERAPY.summary: After spending PP, every allied unit standing in one of the 8 cells adjacent to the caster has its negative-status cooldowns cleared (clearNegativeStatus zeroes the cooldowns; it does NOT clear the wound flag, which is reset later by updateWound in the status update) and is then, in the same synchronous call, healed by raw 20/40/80/160 (by caster stars; AP-scaled, crit only with ability crit). Because the flag is still true when handleHeal runs, a wounded adjacent ally still takes the wound branch: no HP (with BLOODMOON weather and a Blood Stone owned by that ally's player the branch first requests addShield(round(0.3 x stones x the raw requested heal), ally, apBoost 1, crit), with the ally as the shield's caster); the wound only ends at its next status update, so a later cast (or heal) can find it cleared. The same holds for burn: clearNegativeStatus zeroes burnCooldown, but the burn flag stays set until the status update runs updateBurn (which calls healBurn once the cooldown is spent), so a burning adjacent ally's heal in this cast still meets handleHeal's x0.5 burn modifier (probe: heal 20 on HP 100 gives HP 110 for a burning ally and 120 for an ordinary one). An unwounded ally with status.protect gets nothing (Rune Protect alone does not block); otherwise the heal goes through the usual modifiers, rounding and cap, and a GRASS-synergy ally's overheal requests addMaxHP(0.4 x overheal). The caster itself is not in the area (the adjacent-cell list excludes the centre) and nothing moves.

The flag is reset only when updateWound runs in the status update (woundCooldown - dt <= 0 -> wound = false). The heal that follows in the same synchronous callback therefore still sees status.wound = true. Burn behaves the same way: burnCooldown is zeroed but the burn flag stays true until updateBurn runs in the status update (the cooldown branch calls healBurn, which sets burn = false), so handleHeal still applies its x0.5 burn modifier to that heal (probe: burn true, burnCooldown 0 after the cast; HP 100 -> 110 instead of 120).

DRAIN_PUNCH.summary: Single-target SPECIAL damage whose requested amount is the caster's current ATK x a star multiplier (x2 at 1 and 2 stars, x3 at 3, x4 at 4), then the caster requests a heal of 2 x the takenDamage returned by that damage call. takenDamage is the figure handleDamage RETURNS, not universally the HP the target lost: it includes the part absorbed by a shield (flinch splits the reduced hit ceil(50%) / ceil(50%); an attacker's Protective Pads double the shield part), caps the HP part at current HP, is 0 when blocked (protect / skydiving / magic bounce), dead, resurrecting or when Shiny Charm triggers, is extended by the Fossil branch (damage 300 on 500 HP returns 500 with HP unchanged) and is the cover ally's result when a Cover Band holder takes a lethal hit. DREAM_EATER.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare DREAM_EATER (catalog passive NONE). The strategy is shared; differences are star count and stats. The ability has two mutually exclusive branches depending on whether ANY enemy on the board is asleep when it is cast.
DREAM_EATER.summary: Two branches, chosen by scanning the whole board for the first enemy that is asleep. (1) A sleeping enemy exists: the caster moves to a nearest empty neighbour cell of that sleeper if one is free, then deals SPECIAL damage (requested 45 / 90 / 150 / 250 by stars) to that sleeper - not necessarily the cast target - and requests a heal of 1 x the takenDamage that call returned (apBoost 0, crit false). takenDamage is the returned figure (shield part, capped HP part, zero for blocked / dead / Shiny Charm, Fossil extension, cover ally's result), not universally the HP lost. handleHeal is called in this order (core-mechanics.md section J2): the wound branch first - a wounded recipient gets no HP, but with BLOODMOON weather and a Blood Stone owned by its player the same call requests addShield(round(0.3 x stones x the raw requested heal), recipient, apBoost, crit) with the recipient as the shield's caster, which the entity addShield (Big Eater Belt) turns into the final shield; then the guard hp > 0 && !status.protect (an unwounded Protected recipient gets nothing; Rune Protect alone does not block); then the modifiers (AP, crit, BUFF_HEAL_RECEIVED x1.3, burn x0.5, enraged x0.5, ZENITH x1.2), Math.round and the cap at missing HP; the post-modifier overheal on a Grass-synergy recipient requests addMaxHP(0.4 x overheal), which also raises current HP. 'No direct HP healing' therefore does not mean 'no shield or max-HP / current-HP effect'. Requested amount, handleHeal's returned healReceived / overheal and the final stored hp / maxHP / shield are three different things. (2) No enemy is asleep: the code builds targetThatCanSleep = the first of [cast target, then every enemy in board order] that has no Rune Protect, is not skydiving, lacks IMMUNITY_SLEEP and has ccCooldown <= 0. If one is found, sleep is attempted on the ORIGINAL CAST TARGET, not on the enemy that was found, for round([3000, 4000, 5000, 6000][stars - 1] x (1 + AP/100)) ms through triggerSleep, whose own guards (already asleep, Rune Protect, skydiving, IMMUNITY_SLEEP, ccCooldown) can refuse it; and the strategy then assigns pokemon.pp = maxPP directly, whether or not the original target accepted the sleep. If nobody qualifies nothing happens. PP: the base class cost is max(0, pp - maxPP), so the damage branch RETAINS the excess (150 PP with maxPP 100 ends at 50, never 'zero'); the sleep branch overwrites PP with maxPP (100 PP stays 100, 150 PP becomes 100), which is not a universal refund of the cost and does not promise an instant cast (the cast gate and canCast still apply). Requested numbers: DROWZEE (1 star) 45 damage / 3000 ms; HYPNO (2 stars) 90 damage / 4000 ms.

NATURAL_GIFT.summary: Selects the team entity with the lowest hp/maxHP FRACTION (not the lowest absolute hp; the caster is eligible; a tie keeps the first board entry), requests a heal on it and THEN gives it Rune Protect (the heal runs before Rune Protect and so before its cooldown clearing). The heal is a requested 30/60/90 (raw, by stars 1/2/3; 150 for 4 or more) with AP scaling (apBoost 1) and the cast's crit flag; rune protect lasts 1000/2000/3000 ms (6000 for 4+) and its trigger clears the target's listed negative statuses. If the target is wounded the HP heal is 0 (under BLOODMOON weather with a Blood Stone the wound branch requests addShield(round(0.3 x stones x the raw heal)) instead, with the recipient as shield caster) but the Rune Protect is still applied. handleHeal is called in this order (core-mechanics.md section J2): the wound branch first - a wounded recipient gets no HP, but with BLOODMOON weather and a Blood Stone owned by its player the same call requests addShield(round(0.3 x stones x the raw requested heal), recipient, apBoost, crit) with the recipient as the shield's caster, which the entity addShield (Big Eater Belt) turns into the final shield; then the guard hp > 0 && !status.protect (an unwounded Protected recipient gets nothing; Rune Protect alone does not block); then the modifiers (AP, crit, BUFF_HEAL_RECEIVED x1.3, burn x0.5, enraged x0.5, ZENITH x1.2), Math.round and the cap at missing HP; the post-modifier overheal on a Grass-synergy recipient requests addMaxHP(0.4 x overheal), which also raises current HP. 'No direct HP healing' therefore does not mean 'no shield or max-HP / current-HP effect'. Requested amount, handleHeal's returned healReceived / overheal and the final stored hp / maxHP / shield are three different things. Because the heal precedes triggerRuneProtect, whose clearNegativeStatus only zeroes cooldowns, the existing wound AND burn flags are still set when the heal runs and remain set afterwards until their own updates (a burning target's heal is halved). The Rune Protect timer is only raised when the new duration is longer than the remaining one (an existing longer timer is kept). The default cast animation is suppressed and a custom one aimed at the chosen ally is broadcast.

PROTECT.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
PROTECT.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare PROTECT: Deoxys (Defense Forme) (DEOXYS_DEFENSE, 3 stars, maxPP 100, passive ALIEN_DNA) and Kabuto (1 star, maxPP 80, no passive); both range 1. The strategy is shared; unit differences are the star index into the duration table. Units not listed are not covered.
PROTECT.summary: Self-buff. After the base PP spend, the caster gets the Protect status for a requested duration of round(flatDuration x (2 + AP/100) x (crit ? 1 + (critPower - 1) x 0.5 : 1)) ms with flatDuration = [500, 1500, 2500, 4000][stars - 1] (4000 fallback), with table 500 / 1500 / 2500 / 4000 (4000 as fallback) and critFactor 1 + (critPower - 1) x 0.5 when the cast crit, else 1. At AP 0 and no crit that is 1000 ms (Kabuto, 1 star) and 5000 ms (Deoxys Defense, 3 stars); a 1-star caster with AP 100, critPower 2 and a crit requests round(500 x 3 x 1.5) = 2250 ms. triggerProtect does nothing if the caster is already protected (no refresh, no extension) or enraged, so the requested duration is only applied when neither holds. The strategy inherits requiresTarget = true: the cast needs a target in range even though the target is never used. On the paths cited in this record, a protected caster takes no damage from basic attacks (unsuccessful) or ability damage (handleSpecialDamage returns early; handleDamage returns takenDamage 0), positive PP gain is dropped and ordinary healing returns 0 / 0 (the wound branch of handleHeal runs before that guard; core-mechanics.md section J). Those are the paths that were read: this record does not claim that Protect blocks every other status application, forced or voluntary movement, item effect or direct HP writer. Protect is the status.protect flag; Rune Protect (status.runeProtect) is a different flag and neither blocks PP / healing nor implies Protect.

targeting.note: requiresTarget is inherited (true), so the unit must have a target in range to cast; the target parameter is passed to process and used only for the animation coordinates in the base class, never by ProtectStrategy.

effects.scaling: requested duration = round(table[stars-1] x (2 + AP/100) x (crit ? 1 + (critPower - 1) x 0.5 : 1)); the AP factor is 2 + AP/100, so at AP 0 the raw table value is doubled (KABUTO 1000 ms, DEOXYS_DEFENSE 5000 ms). The crit branch needs ABILITY_CRIT because canCritByDefault is false; with critPower 2 the crit factor is 1.5. This is a duration, not a stat or heal amount, so Big Eater Belt and Twist Band do not apply.
effects.resolution: requested duration -> triggerProtect(timer): ignored when the caster is already protected (no refresh) or enraged; otherwise protect = true and protectCooldown = timer. updateProtect(dt) runs on each status update while protect is true and clears the flag when protectCooldown - dt <= 0, so the applied length is the requested duration in simulation time, rounded to update steps. Applied = requested when the guard passes, otherwise nothing.

Ability damage: handleSpecialDamage returns early (spellBlockedCount++) and handleDamage returns death false / takenDamage 0. Positive PP: addPP drops the value (negative PP values are not blocked by this flag). Ordinary healing: handleHeal skips its main branch when hp > 0 and protect is set and returns healReceived 0 / overheal 0; the wound branch earlier in handleHeal is not governed by this flag (core-mechanics.md section J, probe SHARED_HELPERS: Protect returns 0 / 0, Rune Protect alone does not). This is the shared status.protect behaviour; it is not an effect of Rune Protect (a different flag, set by triggerRuneProtect, which triggerProtect does not consult). The five paths listed are the ones read; other damage, status, movement or HP-writing paths were not traced and are not claimed to be blocked.

PSYBEAM.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
PSYBEAM.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare PSYBEAM: Staryu (1 star) and Starmie (2 stars); both range 2, maxPP 100, no passive. The strategy is shared; unit differences are the star index into the damage and confusion-duration tables. Units not listed are not covered.
PSYBEAM.summary: Needs a target (inherited requiresTarget = true). Fires a line from the caster through the cast target to the board edge (effectInLine projects the caster-to-target angle to a point 12 cells away and rounds it; Board.getCellsBetween then walks from the caster's cell, skipping off-board cells: exactly diagonal steps visit only the diagonal cells, not the side cells touched at the corners, e.g. (0,0) toward (2,2) walks (0,0), (1,1), (2,2) and on). Every enemy-team entity on those cells takes requested SPECIAL damage 25 (1 star) / 50 (2 stars) (table 25 / 50 / 100 / 200, 200 as fallback) through handleSpecialDamage with the caster as attacker and the cast's crit flag (crit needs ABILITY_CRIT), then an independent 50% roll (luck-adjusted: p^(1 - luck/100)) triggers confusion of 2000 ms (1 star) / 3000 ms (2 stars) (table 2000 / 3000 / 4000 / 5000, 5000 as fallback) on that enemy. The roll and triggerConfusion happen for every enemy on the line even when the damage call returned 0 (protect / skydiving / Magic Bounce). Protect does not itself block confusion; Rune Protect, an existing confusion and IMMUNITY_CONFUSION (the actual triggerConfusion guards) do. triggerConfusion is called without apBoost, so AP does not scale the duration (2000 / 3000 ms requested); it does nothing on an already confused enemy, with Rune Protect or IMMUNITY_CONFUSION; sandstorm weather multiplies the duration by 1.3, then SWIFT_SWIM / HYDRATION / WATER_VEIL / SURGE_SURFER and Odd Keystone reductions apply; a Persim Berry holder eats the berry (requests: confusion cleared, IMMUNITY_CONFUSION added, heal(50) and addSpecialDefense(10, self, 0, false), each of which passes its own helper before any final value exists), and a target with the PSYDUCK passive requests addAbilityPower(100, self, 0, false) - a request, not a complete account of the PSYDUCK passive.

targeting.who: every enemy-team entity on the line cells; allies and the caster's own cell are skipped by the team filter
targeting.note: The target only fixes the line's angle; effectInLine has no fallback that touches the original target. On the ordinary 8-column x 6-row board the real effectInLine and getCellsBetween reached the target's own cell for all 2256 ordered pairs of distinct positions (enumerated in the probe; not a proof for arbitrary boards). Enemies behind the target are hit too.

geometry.shape: line walked by Board.getCellsBetween from the caster's cell toward the cast target to the board edge (exact diagonals visit only the diagonal cells; oblique lines also visit the cells their horizontal / vertical steps pass through)

effects.scaling: requested = table[stars-1] ?? 200. handleSpecialDamage multiplies by (1 + AP/100) (apBoost default true), x2 once with DOUBLE_DAMAGE, x1.2 with STRANGE_STEAM_BOARD_EFFECT, and on a crit by 1 + (critPower - 1) x the target's crit reduction factor (Rocky Helmet / Black Augurite). Crit needs ABILITY_CRIT because canCritByDefault is false.
effects.resolution: applied = requested after those multipliers, handed to PokemonState.handleDamage: divided by (1 + ARMOR_FACTOR x speDef of the target), rounded up with a minimum of 1, absorbed first by the target's shield. The returned takenDamage is not read by this strategy (how handleDamage builds it, and its exceptions, are in core-mechanics.md section J1); the requested and the applied amount differ. Damage is requested once per enemy on the line.

statusEffects.target: each enemy on the line, per independent roll
statusEffects.scaling: none from AP or crit (apBoost not passed). The chance is chance(0.5, caster): effective probability = 0.5^(1 - luck/100) capped at 1, so luck above 0 raises it.
statusEffects.resolution: triggerConfusion does nothing if the enemy is already confused, has Rune Protect (status.runeProtect) or IMMUNITY_CONFUSION. Otherwise duration x1.3 in SANDSTORM, then SWIFT_SWIM x0.7 (else HYDRATION x0.5, else WATER_VEIL / SURGE_SURFER x0.3), then -10% per Odd Keystone of the enemy's player, rounded; confusion = true and confusionCooldown = that value. Persim Berry holders eat the berry (confusion cleared at once), a PSYDUCK-passive target requests addAbilityPower(100, self, 0, false) - a request, not a guaranteed +100 final AP: addAbilityPower first routes the request to addAttack(round(0.2 x value)) instead when the holder carries a Nullify Bandanna, and otherwise rounds it, applies Big Eater Belt and Twist Band and floors AP at -100 (pokemon-entity.ts:621-647). updateConfusion clears the flag and the unit's target when the cooldown runs out. The roll happens even when the damage was blocked by protect. Requested duration vs applied: the table value is the request, the stored cooldown is the result after the weather and reductions.
statusEffects.guards: triggerConfusion does nothing if the enemy is already confused, has Rune Protect (status.runeProtect) or IMMUNITY_CONFUSION; Protect, damage results and takenDamage are not consulted
statusEffects.applicationOrder: per enemy on the line: damage call first, then an independent chance(0.5, caster) roll (probability 0.5^(1 - luck/100), capped at 1), then triggerConfusion
statusEffects.combatEffect: a confused unit selects its target before the cast / basic-attack decision (attacking-state.ts:33-46 and :92-105): in AttackingState.update an active MERCILESS effect with pp < maxPP takes precedence, otherwise status.confusion calls getTargetWhenConfused (pokemon-state.ts:1302-1340), which draws a luck-adjusted chance(0.5) and, when it is not the bypass outcome, also admits allies and the unit itself among the nearest candidates within range (random pick among ties) - friendly fire is possible but not guaranteed on every action, and a cast uses the target chosen this way; updateConfusion clears the flag and the unit's target on expiry (status.ts:837-844). This is a bounded description, not an imported CONFUSION ability record; here: updateConfusion clears the flag when the cooldown runs out. Persim Berry and the PSYDUCK passive react inside triggerConfusion as requests to their helpers (partial passive information only).

starBehavior.note: Both tables are indexed by the casting entity's stars. The 100 / 200 damage and 4000 / 5000 ms entries are declared in the tables but unused by the two bound baseline classes. Whether other mechanics change a unit's star count was not examined.

PSYBEAM.positionalConditions: Which enemies are hit depends on the caster and target coordinates (angle rounding of the line end point); the enumeration over the ordinary 8x6 board found the cast target's cell on the line in every case. Range 2 only governs when the unit casts; the line itself extends to the board edge.
PSYBEAM.repeatedCastsAndModes: No stored state. Each cast rolls every enemy on the line independently; an enemy already confused is not re-confused (no refresh).
PSYBEAM.rawVsResolved: Declared raw: damage 25 / 50 (STARYU / STARMIE) and confusion 2000 / 3000 ms with chance 0.5. Requested damage = raw x (1 + AP/100) x DOUBLE_DAMAGE x steam x crit factor; applied damage after speDef, minimum 1 and shield. The returned takenDamage is not read by this strategy (section J1). Confusion duration is requested raw (ms, not AP-scaled), then stored after weather, status reductions and Odd Keystones; the stored cooldown (e.g. 2600 ms under sandstorm for a 2000 ms request) is the downstream result. Persim Berry heal / special defense and the PSYDUCK addAbilityPower(100, self, 0, false) are requests whose final results pass their helpers (Big Eater Belt and Nullify Bandanna can alter the AP result).

PSYSHOCK.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare PSYSHOCK: Psyduck (1 star) and Golduck (2 stars); both range 1, maxPP 100, passive PSYDUCK. The strategy is shared; unit differences are the star index into the PP table. Units not listed are not covered.
PSYSHOCK.summary: Needs a target (inherited requiresTarget = true); the default ability animation is suppressed (preventDefaultAnim true). Requested ppBurn = table[stars-1] x (1 + AP/100) with table 20 / 40 / 80 / 160 (160 fallback), not rounded, i.e. 20 (Psyduck) / 40 (Golduck) at AP 0 and 21 for a 1-star caster with AP 5. ppStolen = min(target.pp, ppBurn) and extraPP = ppBurn - ppStolen are both computed BEFORE any PP is removed and are never recomputed: a tree or resurrecting target that drops the loss, or a Twist Band that reverses it, leaves extraPP and the shield request unchanged. The strategy then (1) asks the target to lose ppStolen PP through addPP(-ppStolen, caster, 0, false), (2) gives the caster a shield of the full ppBurn through addShield(ppBurn, caster, 0, false) - not just the stolen part, and (3) if extraPP > 0, deals extraPP as SPECIAL damage to the target through handleSpecialDamage with the cast's crit flag and apBoost false (AP is already inside ppBurn). Requested, downstream and stored amounts differ: addPP rounds -ppStolen and may be dropped (status.tree, resurrecting) or turned positive (Twist Band on the target; a positive value is then also subject to silence / protect / NO_PP_GAIN); the entity addShield first applies Big Eater Belt (x1.25 with a floor) on the caster, then the state's addShield halves a positive value when the caster is enraged, then applies Math.round (ppBurn 21: 21 plain, 11 enraged because 10.5 rounds up, 26 with a Belt, 13 with a Belt and enraged), and needs the caster alive; addPP computes the request in this order (pokemon-entity.ts:508-532): value = round(base x (1 + apBoost x caster.AP/100) x crit factor x (fatigue AND base > 0 ? 0.5 : 1)) - Math.round applies to a request of either sign and only the fatigue multiplier depends on base > 0 (executed: PP 10 with addPP(-2.5, enemy, 0, false) gives PP 8, because Math.round(-2.5) = -2); then applyTwistBandBuff (a Twist Band holder hit by an enemy turns a negative value positive); then the guards on the RESULTING value: a positive result is dropped by silence, status.protect or NO_PP_GAIN, any result is dropped while resurrecting, and a negative result is dropped by status.tree. So Protect does not block a negative loss, fatigue is not applied to a negative request or to a gain flipped by Twist Band, and a flipped gain faces the positive-gain guards; crit applies only to the excess damage and no second AP factor applies to the shield or the excess damage; the excess damage is divided by the target's special defence, rounded up with a minimum of 1 and takes the shield first; a Magic Bounce target blocks it (returned takenDamage 0) and queues a delayed reflection only when the damage is positive and the attacker does not hold Protective Pads.

effects.resolution: addPP(-ppStolen): value = Math.round(-ppStolen x 1 x 1 x 1) (fatigue only halves positive requests, so it does not apply to the negative request); applyTwistBandBuff then flips the rounded value to positive for a Twist Band holder when the caster is an enemy - fatigue was applied (or not) before it, only to a positive request, so the flipped gain is not halved; the guards then run on the resulting value (resurrecting blocks any result, tree blocks a resulting negative, silence / Protect / NO_PP_GAIN block a resulting positive); a negative value is dropped while the target has status.tree or is resurrecting; the final pp = clamp(pp + value, 0, 2 x maxPP - 1). Status.protect does not block a negative value (it blocks positive PP gain; section J3). Applied = the rounded value when not dropped; with a fractional ppBurn the rounding means the target loses the rounded amount while the shield and extraPP use the unrounded number. Twist Band reverses the effect into a PP gain for the target if it is not silenced, protected or under NO_PP_GAIN.

PSYSTRIKE.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare PSYSTRIKE: Mewtwo and Shadow Mewtwo (both 3 stars, maxPP 110, range 3, no passive). The strategy is shared; both listed units are identical in stars, so they share the same raw damage. Units not listed are not covered.
PSYSTRIKE.summary: Needs a target (inherited requiresTarget = true). The line end is the farthest TARGETTABLE unit by Manhattan distance (board scan row by row, the first at the maximum wins), or the cast target when none is found. 'Targettable' here is isTargettableBy(caster): enemies, and also - for a caster with the MERCILESS effect - allies with hp <= 10; both bound Mewtwo forms declare the MONSTER synergy and MONSTER's effects include MERCILESS (applied to MONSTER-typed entities when the team's tier is active), so the endpoint is not universally an enemy. Every ENEMY-team entity on the supercover line from the caster's cell to that unit (both endpoints) is collected; if none, the farthest unit is inserted WITHOUT checking its team (a conditional ally-damage fallback: executed with a 5-hp ally under MERCILESS; intent not guessed). Each collected enemy takes requested SPECIAL damage 80 (both listed units are 3 stars; table 20 / 40 / 80 / 160, 160 fallback) through handleSpecialDamage with the cast's crit flag (crit needs ABILITY_CRIT), and right after its own damage call the unit is moved (requested as forced displacement) to the free cell, among the cells on the lines from its position to the two back corners of its own team's side, that is farthest by Chebyshev distance. The movement is requested after the damage call with no check that the damage succeeded or that the unit survived or is still on the board; Protect does not block the movement primitive; a locked, skydiving or Heavy Duty Boots unit is not moved, and nothing is moved when no free destination exists. Do not read this as a promise of successful teleportation after lethal damage or removal (the probe's lethal case is a controlled callback that sets hp to 0).

targeting.note: The line end does not come from the cast target but from getFarthestTarget (Manhattan distance, strictly greater, scan order); the cast target is used only when that returns undefined. The caster's own cell is on the line but filtered out as same-team; allies standing on the line are skipped by the filter, but an ally that is itself the endpoint can be inserted by the empty-set fallback.

Crit needs ABILITY_CRIT.

The returned takenDamage is not read by this strategy (how handleDamage builds it, and its exceptions, are in core-mechanics.md section J1); the requested and the applied amount differ.

effects.resolution: getTeleportationCell collects the free cells on the supercover lines from the enemy's current cell to its team's two back-row corners, sorts by Chebyshev distance from the enemy (greatest first, ties in collection order) and returns the first; undefined when no free cell exists. moveTo(…, true) returns without moving when the unit cannot be moved (skydiving, locked, Heavy Duty Boots) or the destination holds a unit that cannot be moved; otherwise the unit goes to its moving state, the cells are swapped and its cooldown is set to 100. Protect is not consulted. No survival or success check precedes the request. Enemies are processed in insertion (line) order, so earlier teleports change which cells are free for later ones, and the enemy's position is read after its own damage.

PSYSHIELD_BASH.summary: Needs a target in range (inherited requiresTarget = true). Asks the board helper getFarthestTargetCoordinateAvailablePlace for a destination: normally a free cell next to the farthest targettable enemy (Manhattan distance, not necessarily the cast target), but the helper keeps the cell chosen for an EARLIER nearer enemy when a farther enemy has no free adjacent cell (retained-earlier-cell case), and only when no cell was selected at all does it fall back to the closest free cell to the farthest enemy, which need not be adjacent (executed: retained cell (4,1) next to the nearer enemy; fallback (7,3), two cells from the enemy at (7,5)). If a destination exists, the enemies standing on the supercover line from the caster's current cell to that destination are collected (before the caster moves), then the caster moves there with moveTo(x, y, board, false): an unforced self-move that does not consult canBeMoved (executed: a locked caster holding Heavy Duty Boots still moves). Regardless of whether a destination existed, after the movement opportunity and before any damage the caster requests Protect for a fixed 1000 ms (no AP or crit scaling; an existing Protect is not refreshed and an enraged caster gets none). If the hit set is empty - no destination, or no enemy on the line - the ORIGINAL CAST TARGET is added without another team check (executed with an ally as the cast target and with an off-line enemy). Each collected enemy takes requested SPECIAL damage 50 (Stantler, 3 stars) / 60 (Wyrdeer, 4 stars) (table 30 / 40 / 50 / 60 / 120, fallback 120) via handleSpecialDamage with the caster as attacker and the cast's crit flag (crit needs ABILITY_CRIT).

RAPID_SPIN.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare RAPID_SPIN: Phanpy (1 star) and Donphan (2 stars). The strategy is shared; unit differences are the star count (damage table index), atk (the buff base), range and maxPP. Units not listed are not covered.
RAPID_SPIN.summary: Deals SPECIAL damage (raw 20/50/100/200 by the caster's stars) to the cast target, then gives the caster +DEF and +SPE_DEF of the same requested size, Math.round(0.5 x the caster's current atk at cast time), a value that grows with atk rather than a star table. The buff amount is sampled BEFORE the damage call (atk is read once, so a change of atk during or after the hit does not alter it) and the buffs are unconditional: they are made whether the damage call dealt damage or returned 0. The ability never reads the damage call's returned value; AP/crit rounding and a held Big Eater Belt are applied afterwards by the stat adders (Twist Band cannot change a positive self buff).

REFLECT.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
REFLECT.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare REFLECT: Espurr (1 star) and Meowstic male (2 stars). The strategy is shared; unit differences are the star count (the reflect factor index) and stats. Espurr also declares the passive ESPURR, which is not covered here. Meowstic female and other units are not covered.
REFLECT.summary: Self-targeted status cast: the caster gains the reflect status for 3000 ms (stars 1-3; 5000 ms from 4 stars) via Status.triggerReflect. While reflect is active, a PHYSICAL hit that reaches the reflect branch of PokemonState.handleDamage is negated: the function returns death false / takenDamage 0 and nothing is dealt to the reflector. That branch is reached only after the earlier guards - a dead or resurrecting recipient returns first, and protect / skydiving return takenDamage 0 BEFORE it (no reflection in those cases) - and after the attacker-side multipliers. Whether the hit is reflected is a separate question: unless the attacker is absent, holds Protective Pads or the hit is itself a retaliation, the attacker receives, through attacker.handleDamage (not handleSpecialDamage) as SPECIAL damage with isRetaliation true, equal to round(factor x the incoming damage x (1 + the reflector's AP/100) x critPower if the reflector's ABILITY_CRIT roll succeeds), factor 0.5 / 0.75 / 1 / 1.5 by the reflector's stars (so 0.5 for Espurr, 0.75 for Meowstic). No damage is dealt by the cast itself. Recasting while active only extends the timer to the larger value.

targeting.who: the caster itself; the cast target is only the generic requiresTarget gate
targeting.note: The strategy never reads target. Reflected damage goes to whoever attacks the reflecting unit with PHYSICAL damage during the window.

effects.scaling: No AP scaling and no duration reduction: triggerReflect(timer) stores the timer as is. The cooldown only rises (if timer > current, replace); a second cast does not stack.
effects.resolution: reflect = true until the cooldown counted down by updateReflect reaches 0. Not blocked by Rune Protect (triggerReflect has no runeProtect check). Ended early by RAGING_BULL, BRICK_BREAK or SHADOW_FORCE against the unit.

effects.target: the attacker of any PHYSICAL hit on the reflecting unit

declaredRaw.label: reflect factor by the reflecting unit's stars (raw multiplier of the incoming damage)

effects.scaling: reflected = Math.round(factor x damage x (1 + AP/100) x (critPower if reflectCrit)); damage is the incoming physical figure after the enraged / field / weather / Hisuian Typhlosion / Sheer Cold multipliers and BEFORE the defense division; AP and crit are the reflecting unit's own; reflectCrit needs the ABILITY_CRIT effect and a roll of its critChance.
effects.resolution: the reflected figure is sent to attacker.handleDamage as SPECIAL, so it is then reduced by the attacker's SPE_DEF (armor reduction halves it), has minimum 1 and can hit a shield. Skipped (nothing reflected) if the attacker holds Protective Pads, or the hit is a retaliation (isRetaliation). For an eligible PHYSICAL hit that reaches the reflect branch, the original hit returns takenDamage 0 and deals nothing to the reflecting unit whether or not a reflection is generated (no-reflection cases: attacker holds Protective Pads, the hit is a retaliation, or there is no attacker); a protect / skydiving / dead / resurrecting recipient returns earlier and also reflects nothing; SPECIAL and TRUE hits are neither negated nor reflected by this branch. The reflection goes to attacker.handleDamage directly, so it does not pass handleSpecialDamage's AP / crit stage; the AP and crit figures are the reflector's own, in the reflect formula. A Human-synergy heal effect from the reflected damage is also triggered (not traced further).

SCREECH.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
SCREECH.scope: KRICKETOT (1 star) and KRICKETUNE (2 stars) declare SCREECH (passive NONE, maxPP 60, range 1). The strategy is shared; only the debuff amount depends on the casting unit's stars. Units not listed are not covered.
SCREECH.summary: Area defense debuff centred on the CASTER (not the target): every enemy within radius 2 of the caster (getCellsInRadius, strict squared distance < 6.25 from the caster's cell, caster cell excluded; off-board cells skipped - offset (2,1) is inside, (2,2) outside) has addDefense(debuff, caster, 1, crit) called, with a requested raw change of -2 / -4 / -8 / -16 by caster stars (KRICKETOT -2, KRICKETUNE -4). No damage is dealt. The requested amount is modified by addDefense before it is stored: value = Math.round(value x (1 + caster AP/100) x (critPower only if the cast crit; canCritByDefault is false so only with ABILITY_CRIT)), so AP makes the debuff more negative. Then the Big Eater Belt helper does nothing for an enemy holder (it scales only positive values and negative values from the holder's own team), but the Twist Band helper flips a negative value from another team into a positive one, so an enemy holding Twist Band gains DEF by the absolute amount instead of losing it. Finally target.def = max(0, def + value): DEF cannot go below 0. This strategy installs no timer and no restore step: permanent = false only means the board unit is not modified (only the fight entity), it does not make the debuff a timed one, and other code that resets stats was not audited. Requested amount (table), applied change (after AP, crit, Twist Band, and the floor at 0) are different amounts. No heal, PP gain or shield is involved, so the shared heal rules (core-mechanics.md section J) do not apply.

SHEER_COLD.summary: Single-target SPECIAL hit on the cast target with a chance to replace the damage by 9999. Normal raw damage 50/100/200/400 by caster stars (50 for SNOVER, 100 for ABOMASNOW). executeChance = base 0.1/0.2/0.3/0.6 by stars x (1 + min(0)((casterHP - targetHP) / targetHP)) where this codebase's min(0)(x) is Math.max(0, x), i.e. max(0, ...) (factor 1 when the caster has no more HP than the target); it is set to 0 if the target has the ICE synergy type, else to 1 if the target is frozen (status.freeze). chance() rolls it with the caster's luck as exponent (p^(1 - luck/100), cap 1; probability 0 never succeeds, probability 1 always does). On success the requested raw damage is 9999, otherwise the table value. Either goes through handleSpecialDamage as SPECIAL with the cast crit flag and apBoost true, so AP, crit, SPE_DEF division, shields and protect apply: 9999 is the requested amount, not a guaranteed kill. The returned takenDamage is ignored (section J1 lists its exceptions); 9999 is a requested amount that still passes AP, crit, SPE_DEF, shields and the block guards.

SOLAR_BEAM.scope: The units in appliesTo declare SOLAR_BEAM in this production reference. The strategy is shared; differences are star count (damage), max HP, maxPP and the entity's stats.
SOLAR_BEAM.summary: The caster fires a line from its own cell toward the cast target and on to the board edge: effectInLine projects the angle to a point 12 cells away and rounds that end point, then Board.getCellsBetween walks from the caster's cell to it, skipping off-board cells. Exactly diagonal steps visit ONLY the diagonal cells: (0,0) toward (2,2) walks (0,0), (1,1), (2,2) and on (3,3), (4,4), (5,5), never the side cells (1,0) or (0,1); an oblique line also visits the cells its horizontal / vertical steps pass through, e.g. (0,0) toward (2,1) walks (0,0), (1,0), (1,1), (2,1), (3,1), (3,2), (4,2), (5,2), (6,3), (7,3) (executed on an 8 x 6 stand-in board). Every enemy-team unit on those cells is burned for 3000 ms and then takes SPECIAL damage (raw 25/50/100/200 by caster stars; SUNKERN 1 star -> 25, SUNFLORA 2 stars -> 50). If the simulation weather is ZENITH or the caster has the light status (status.light, set for units in the spotlight by the light effects), the raw damage is multiplied by 1.3 (25 -> 32.5, 50 -> 65, not rounded here) and the caster first requests +20 PP (addPP, apBoost 0, no crit) - after the base PP spend and before any line effect, even if no enemy is on the line. Requested vs applied: the +20 PP is requested; the applied change is after addPP's rules: fatigue halves positive gains, nothing is gained while the caster is silenced, status.protect (Rune Protect alone does not block it), NO_PP_GAIN or resurrecting, and PP is clamped to 0..2 x maxPP - 1; the PP spend of the cast (super.process) already happened. Damage is requested raw x 1.3 (conditional) x (1 + AP/100) [x crit factor], then the target's special-defense division (ceil, min 1) and shields in handleDamage. The returned takenDamage is not read by this ability (shield part, Shiny Charm, Fossil and Cover Band accounting is in core-mechanics.md section J1). The burn is not AP-scaled; it replaces a running burn timer only if longer, is blocked by IMMUNITY_BURN, Rune Protect or the WATER_BUBBLE passive on the victim, and then deals TRUE damage of 5 % of the victim's max HP per tick (weather is not always a reduction: DROUGHT multiplies it by 1.3 and only then do Heat Rocks reduce it, RAIN multiplies it by 0.7; Assault Vest x0.5; SWIFT_SWIM x0.7, HYDRATION x0.5, WATER_VEIL / SURGE_SURFER x0.3; none for WELL_BAKED or Magmarizer; a Cooking Pot holder also gains 10 speed per tick; executed on maxHP 1000: 50 / DROUGHT 65 / one Heat Rock 52 / two 39 / RAIN 35). triggerBurn has no protect check, so the burn can land even when protect blocks the damage.

SPLASH.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare SPLASH: Magikarp (1 star, maxPP 50, passive MAGIKARP) and Feebas (1 star, maxPP 100, passive FEEBAS). Units are bound by the queue record only. The passives named in appliesTo are separate records and are not covered here.
SPLASH.summary: Cast with no effect of its own. SplashStrategy.process only calls super.process (base process: spends maxPP of PP, increments count.ult, broadcasts the default ability animation with target coordinates -1/-1 when there is no target, records the skill in the team's cast list) and then does nothing; the source comment says this is intentional. requiresTarget is false, so the cast can fire from the moving state with no target once pp >= maxPP and canCast. castAbility returns before anything when canCast is false (no PP is spent); otherwise it rolls the crit (only with ABILITY_CRIT), runs process and then ALWAYS runs the OnAbilityCastEffect hooks with the same target (null from the moving state) and crit flag, so a held item or synergy effect that reacts to ability casts can still act on a SPLASH cast (executed with a stand-in hook: it ran once, after the base bookkeeping). No damage, heal, shield, PP gain, status or stat change is made by the strategy.

targeting.who: none; the strategy ignores the target parameter (typed null) and the cast target is null when cast from the moving state
targeting.note: requiresTarget = false overrides the base default true, so the unit does not have to walk up to an enemy to cast. If the cast happens in the attacking state a target exists and is passed through to the base process, which uses it only for the animation coordinates.

declaredRaw.note: no amount is declared in splash.ts

effects.scaling: none: nothing is requested, so there is no requested or applied amount of its own, and no AP, crit, stat helper, Big Eater Belt, Twist Band or Rune Protect interaction exists for this strategy
effects.resolution: The only state changes are the base-process bookkeeping: pp = max(0, pp - maxPP), count.ult + 1, the animation broadcast and the team's cast list entry. This is a spend of the unit's own PP, not a PP gain, so the addPP guards (status.protect) do not apply to it.

SUPER_FANG.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare SUPER_FANG: Bidoof (1 star, maxPP 90) and Bibarel (2 stars, maxPP 80), range 1, no passive. Units are bound by the queue record only.
SUPER_FANG.summary: Single-target TRUE damage proportional to the target's maximum HP. Requested amount = ceil(fraction x target.maxHP x (2 + AP/100)) with fraction 10 % / 15 % / 25 % / 35 % by the caster's stars (fallback 35 %); the AP is already inside this formula and handleSpecialDamage is called with apBoost = false, so it is not applied twice. The cast crit flag is passed on (crit only with ABILITY_CRIT). TRUE damage skips the defense division but still passes the ceil and floor-of-1 step in handleDamage; shields absorb first. The returned takenDamage is unused (section J1). Executed on a target with maxHP 1000: 1 star AP 0 requests 200 (twice the 10 %), AP 100 requests 300 (three times), 2 stars AP 0 requests 300; maxHP 1234 with AP 50 -> ceil(308.5) = 309.

targeting.note: requiresTarget keeps the base default true, so the caster walks to range before casting.

effects.scaling: requested = ceil(fraction x target maxHP x (2 + AP/100)); with AP 0 that is twice the fraction of max HP (20 % for 1 star, 30 % for 2 stars). downstream request into handleDamage: handleSpecialDamage adds no AP (apBoost false), doubles it if the caster has DOUBLE_DAMAGE (consumed), multiplies by 1.2 with the strange-steam board effect, and on a crit by 1 + (critPower - 1) x critReductionFactor (for TRUE damage neither Rocky Helmet nor Black Augurite reduces the crit, so the factor is 1 + (critPower - 1) and the target's crit counter always increments). handleDamage then applies no defense division to TRUE damage, but the ceil and floor of 1 still apply (core-mechanics section A), and a shield absorbs first; the returned takenDamage is unused (section J1). Protect, skydiving or magic bounce on the target return takenDamage 0; a magic bounce reflects only SPECIAL type damage, so nothing is reflected here, and a Power Lens only retaliates against SPECIAL type.
effects.resolution: requested ceil(fraction x maxHP x (2 + AP/100)) -> downstream request after DOUBLE_DAMAGE / crit factors -> final HP loss after shield absorption, Protect, and the section J1 exceptions (Shiny Charm, Fossil, Cover Band); the strategy uses none of the returned amounts

Downstream: no second AP, crit factor only if the cast crits (ABILITY_CRIT), DOUBLE_DAMAGE x2. Final: no defense reduction, ceil and floor of 1, shield first, then HP; blocked by Protect or skydiving. The base is the target's maximum HP, not its current HP.

TAILWIND.scope: DRIFLOON (1 star) and DRIFBLIM (2 stars), the queued units. Ability.TAILWIND only: the identically named EffectEnum.TAILWIND (a Flying synergy effect) is a different mechanic and is not described here.
TAILWIND.summary: Team-wide speed buff: every entity on the board that is on the caster's team (the caster included, no range or distance test) receives addSpeed(buff, caster, 1, crit), with buff 5 at 1 star, 10 at 2, 15 at 3, 30 at 4+ (DRIFLOON 5, DRIFBLIM 10, raw). For each recipient the value is first adjusted by its own Big Eater Belt helper (x1.25 rounded down to an integer), then scaled by the caster's AP (x (1 + AP/100)) and by critPower if the cast crit, with no rounding (executed: AP 50 on 5 -> speed 57.5), and added to its speed clamped to 0..300. A recipient with the MELMETAL passive instead gets addAttack(0.5 x the Belt-adjusted value, caster, apBoost 1, crit): addAttack applies the caster's AP and crit, ROUNDS (Math.round), runs the Belt and Twist helpers AGAIN and floors ATK at 1; its speed never changes (executed, AP 0, no crit: 1 star 5 -> 2.5 -> 3 ATK, 2 stars 10 -> 5 ATK; with a Belt 1 star 5 -> 6 -> 3 -> 3 ATK, 2 stars 10 -> 12 -> 6 -> 7 ATK; AP 100 with a crit at 2 stars 5 x 2 x 2 = 20 ATK). The buff is not timed; it lasts for the fight. Requires no target.

effects.target: every ally on the board including the caster

effects.scaling: per recipient, in this order inside addSpeed(value, caster, apBoost 1, crit): Big Eater Belt of the RECIPIENT (value x1.25 rounded down, e.g. 5 -> 6, 10 -> 12), Twist Band (no effect on a positive value), then x (1 + caster AP/100) and x caster critPower if the cast crit (needs ABILITY_CRIT; canCritByDefault is false); no Math.round, so fractional speed is possible; result added to speed and clamped to 0..MAX_SPEED (300)
effects.resolution: applied change per ally = the figure above, limited by the clamp at 300; allies with the MELMETAL passive get addAttack(value x 0.5, caster, 1, crit) instead, with the value already Belt-adjusted: addAttack applies AP and crit, rounds with Math.round, runs the Belt and Twist helpers again and floors ATK at 1 (see the summary for the executed values). The AP and crit scaling use the CASTER's ap and critPower for every ally; the recipient's own AP does not matter

starBehavior.note: amount indexed by the caster's stars (pokemon.stars - 1), fallback 30; 15 and 30 are not reached by these units. maxPP 100 and range 2 for both (range only affects when the unit can attack; the buff has no range).

TAIL_WHIP.summary: Single-target DEF reduction. The requested loss is a percentage of the target's CURRENT DEF at cast time: 20% at 1 star, 30% at 2, 40% at 3, 50% at 4+ (ALOLAN_RATTATA 20%, ALOLAN_RATICATE 30%), passed as a negative number to target.addDefense(defLoss, caster, 1, crit). addDefense then scales the (negative) amount by (1 + AP/100) and by critPower if the cast crit, rounds it, and applies the Big Eater Belt / Twist Band helpers of the TARGET: an enemy's reduction is not boosted by Big Eater Belt, but a Twist Band holder turns it into a gain of the same size. DEF cannot go below 0. Executed on a target with DEF 10: 1 star requests -2 (DEF 8), 2 stars -3; the request is rounded by addDefense with Math.round, so 30 % of DEF 5 is -1.5 which rounds to -1 (DEF 4), and 20 % of DEF 2 is -0.4 which rounds to 0 (no change at AP 0; AP 100 makes it -0.8 -> -1). No damage, no duration (the change stays for the fight).

dispatch.note: No overrides: base defaults apply (target required, crit only with the ABILITY_CRIT effect). The target is used only for its team (target.team).

TICKLE.summary: After spending PP, the strategy takes the living units of the target's team sorted by Chebyshev distance from the CASTER's cell (stable sort: ties keep the board's cells-array order, which is row-major), keeps the first 1/2/3/5 by caster stars (1 for Aipom, 2 for Ambipom) and applies to each of them addAttack(-3, caster, apBoost 1, crit) and addDefense(-3, caster, apBoost 1, crit). The three is a RAW request: each helper multiplies it by (1 + caster AP/100) and, on a crit, by critPower, rounds it (Math.round), and then applies the holder's items. The chosen enemies are the closest ones to the caster, which is not necessarily the unit being attacked (target.team is the only thing read from the cast target; for an ordinary enemy cast target that is the enemy team. Executed with a same-team stand-in target: the nearest unit of THAT team, here the caster itself at distance 0, is selected instead and the enemy is not; whether a cast target can be on the caster's own team in a real fight was not examined). Executed on an 8 x 6 stand-in board (caster at (3,3)): 1 star hits only the nearest, 2 stars the two nearest, 5 stars five of six; dead (hp 0) units and allies are skipped; Chebyshev, not Manhattan (units at (5,5) and (5,4), distance 2, come before one at (6,3), distance 3); among four enemies at distance 1 the first two in row-major cell order (above, then left) are hit; ATK 20 / DEF 10 become 17 / 7, AP 100 or a crit give 14 / 4, ATK 2 floors at 1 and DEF 1 at 0, a Twist Band holder gains (23 / 13). Nothing is restored afterwards: the changes last for the rest of the fight. Attack cannot fall below 1 and Defense cannot fall below 0 (the clamp, not the request, bounds the applied change).

TOXIC.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare the ability TOXIC: Tentacool (1 star) and Tentacruel (2 stars); both maxPP 85, range 1, no declared passive. The strategy is shared; the unit difference is the star count. Routing: see the NAME_SHARED_WITH_EFFECT note.

dispatch.note: No overrides: base defaults (target required, crit only with ABILITY_CRIT). Routing uncertainty NAME_SHARED_WITH_EFFECT: the string TOXIC also names EffectEnum.TOXIC, a different enum member used by the Poison synergy (top tier). The unit's skill is Ability.TOXIC and the registry maps that key to ToxicStrategy; the effect enum is never consulted for dispatch. The effect only matters inside triggerPoison, where an origin (the caster) that has EffectEnum.TOXIC raises the poison stack cap to 5.

TOXIC.summary: After spending PP, the strategy takes the living enemies (the target's team) sorted by Chebyshev distance from the CASTER, keeps the first 1/2/3/4 by caster stars (1 for Tentacool, 2 for Tentacruel) and calls triggerPoison(duration, enemy, caster) ONCE on each - one poison stack per selected enemy per cast. The requested duration is round(flat x (2 + AP/100) x critFactor) with flat 1500/3000/4500/9000 ms by stars (so 3000 / 6000 ms at AP 0 for these units) and critFactor 1 + (critPower - 1) x 0.5 only on an ability crit (crit needs the ABILITY_CRIT effect). Inside triggerPoison: the call does nothing if the enemy has IMMUNITY_POISON or Rune Protect; otherwise poisonOrigin = caster, stacks + 1 up to 3 (4 if the caster has VENOMOUS, 5 if the caster has the synergy effect EffectEnum.TOXIC), the duration passes through the enemy's reductions (Swift Swim x0.7, else Hydration x0.5, else Water Veil / Surge Surfer x0.3; then Odd Keystone x(1 - 0.1 n) of the enemy's player), the poison timer is raised only if the new duration is longer than the remaining one (durations do not add), and reactions can fire: GUTS adds +5 ATK once (addAttack request, flag GUTS_PASSIVE), TOXIC_BOOST +10 ATK once, and a PECHA_BERRY holder eats the berry (the berry's own text heals, clears the poison stacks and origin and adds IMMUNITY_POISON; source reading). The poison tick (Status.updatePoison, executed on maxHP 1000) deals TRUE damage of round(5 % max HP x stacks) every 1000 ms, at least 1: RAIN x0.7, Assault Vest x0.5, the TOXIC_BOOST passive x0.5, SWIFT_SWIM x0.7 / HYDRATION x0.5 / WATER_VEIL or SURGE_SURFER x0.3; a GLISCOR uses stacks - 2 (1 stack heals 50, 2 stacks nothing); the POISON_GAS field re-applies a stack each tick unless the unit wears Heavy Duty Boots. Executed requests: 1 star 3000 ms (double the flat 1500 at AP 0), 2 stars 6000 ms, AP 100 4500 ms, a crit 4500 ms (half-strength crit factor 1.5), 2 stars with AP 100 and a crit 13500 ms; one triggerPoison per selected enemy.

WATERFALL.scope: GOLDEEN (1 star) and SEAKING (2 stars), the queued units.
WATERFALL.summary: Self-only effect, no damage and no target. In order the caster (1) requests a shield of 50 (GOLDEEN, 1 star) or 100 (SEAKING, 2 stars) through pokemon.addShield(shield, pokemon, 1, crit), (2) calls status.clearNegativeStatus(caster, caster) and (3) calls board.clearBoardEffect on its own current cell with no specific effect, clearing every board effect there. The shield amount is the REQUESTED value: the entity method first multiplies a positive value by 1.25 rounded down when the caster holds a Big Eater Belt, then the state method multiplies by (1 + AP/100) (apBoost 1), by critPower on a crit, by 0.5 when the caster is enraged, rounds, and adds it to the current shield (floor 0), only if the caster's hp > 0. addShield is not healing: Protect (status.protect), wound and Rune Protect do not appear in it (shared references: core-mechanics section J4 for the addShield path, J2 for what handleHeal guards). clearNegativeStatus zeroes the cooldowns of burn, silence, fatigue, poison, freeze, sleep, confusion, wound, paralysis, charm, flinch, armor reduction, locked and blinded, clears curse (and adds 2000 ms to a running curse cooldown instead of zeroing it) and zeroes the possession cooldown unless the caster is possessed (the origin passed is the caster itself, so origin.team === entity.team always holds and ANY active possession keeps its cooldown); the boolean flags themselves drop on each status's next update. The status cleansing and the board-effect clear are separate mechanisms: clearBoardEffect removes EVERY board effect registered on the caster's own cell (harmful or helpful) from the cell and from the caster's effects set, whereas clearNegativeStatus touches neither effects nor the boolean flags. Executed (stand-in units): order shield -> clearNegativeStatus -> clearBoardEffect; shield 50 / 100 (AP 100 or a crit doubles it, Belt 62, enraged 25, hp 0 -> 0); the 14 cooldowns zero while burn / poison / paralysis flags and 3 poison stacks stay set; curse cooldown 3000 -> 5000; an active possession keeps its cooldown. The cast needs no target.

effects.resolution: applied change: shield = max(0, shield + round(value)), only when the caster's hp > 0 (otherwise nothing is added); shieldDone is credited to the caster. Requested (50 / 100) versus applied (after Belt, AP, crit, enraged halving, rounding) differ whenever one of those applies. Not subject to the heal guards: Protect, wound and Rune Protect do not block a shield. The shield later absorbs damage inside handleDamage (core-mechanics section J1); no timer on the shield was found in this strategy.

It sets cooldowns to 0 and the curse flag to false; a running curse cooldown gets +2000 ms instead of being zeroed ('do not clear curseCooldown on purpose'); the possession cooldown is zeroed unless the unit is possessed: the origin passed here is the caster itself, so origin.team === entity.team always holds and ANY active possession keeps its cooldown. It does not set the boolean flags (burn, paralysis, ...) or poisonStacks: each flag falls when its update function next sees cooldown - dt <= 0 (e.g. confusion and armor reduction on the next update; poison stacks reset at the end of updatePoison, after that call's poison damage block) so the cleansing is effective at the caster's next status update, not instantly inside the cast. Positive statuses are untouched.

YAWN.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
YAWN.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare YAWN: Slowpoke (1 star, passive SLOWPOKE) and Slowbro (2 stars, no passive); both maxPP 100, range 1. The strategy is shared; unit differences are the star count (shield table index) and speed (cooldown reset). Slowking is not listed and does not declare YAWN in the pinned unit blocks.
YAWN.summary: Without needing a target: every enemy that currently has the caster as its target gets a 3000 ms fatigue request (halves its positive PP gains) and an AP change of -20 (request; Twist Band flips it, Nullify Bandanna turns it into -4 ATK, AP is clamped at -100). Then the caster gains a shield (raw 15/30/60/120 by stars: 15 Slowpoke, 30 Slowbro) and resetCooldown(1000) stores round(1000 / (0.4 + speed x 0.007)) ms in the caster's cooldown field (speed 35 -> 1550, speed 100 -> 909), a stored number only: AttackingState.update already stores the same formula just before casting, and how the stored value changes the unit's next action in a fight was not simulated. The two parts run per enemy in this order: fatigue first, then the AP change, and the AP change still happens when the fatigue is refused (Rune Protect refuses only the fatigue); a Nullify Bandanna holder takes addAttack(round(0.2 x -20) = -4) instead and a holder that also wears a Twist Band GAINS 4 ATK (executed: ATK 20 -> 16, with a Twist Band 24; a Twist Band alone turns -20 AP into +20; AP -90 floors at -100). The AP and fatigue parts are not damage and have no AP/crit scaling.

MEDITATE.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare MEDITATE: Meditite (1 star, atk 9) and Medicham (2 stars, atk 16); both maxPP 100, range 2, no passive. The strategy is shared; the difference is the unit's base attack (the buff amount scales with it). MEDITATE as an ability is distinct from EffectEnum.MEDITATE, the HUMAN synergy tier-1 effect (see routing).

dispatch.registry: AbilityStrategies[Ability.MEDITATE] = meditateStrategy (exported constant instance of the unexported class MeditateStrategy)

MEDITATE.summary: Needs no target and deals no damage. The caster raises its own attack by its baseAtk (the attack it had when the combat entity was created), scaled by (1 + AP/100) and by its critPower if the cast crits, rounded, then adjusted by its own Big Eater Belt if held, and added to its current attack (attack cannot fall below 1). The request is the combat entity's baseAtk, copied from the board Pokemon's atk when the entity is created (pokemon-entity.ts:178): not the entity's current atk and not a field of the bare-unit data. The catalog values 9 (Meditite) and 16 (Medicham) are examples that hold only when the board Pokemon had its catalog atk; any acquired modifier folded into that atk changes the request. Executed: baseAtk 9 on current atk 20 -> 29, two casts -> 38 (the fixed snapshot is added each time), current atk 40 -> 49 (not doubled). The change is not temporary in code: addAttack has no timer and permanent is false, so it lasts for the combat only, and each cast adds again.

Crit is rolled by castAbility only if the caster has ABILITY_CRIT (canCritByDefault is false). permanent = false: the board Pokemon is not changed. No expiry is coded in the strategy or in addAttack.

FAIRY_WIND.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
FAIRY_WIND.scope: The 15 units in appliesTo (Flabebe, Floette, Florges and their Blue/Orange/White/Yellow forms) declare ABILITY FAIRY_WIND. EffectEnum.FAIRY_WIND (Fairy synergy tier effect) shares the name but is a different mechanism and is NOT covered. Their passive FLABEBE_COLOR is a separate queue record.
FAIRY_WIND.summary: Gives PP to every allied unit on the board except the caster. The amount is a per-star base (2.5/5/10/20 for 1/2/3/4 stars) multiplied by (2 + AP/100), then rounded inside addPP. The AP term is already inside the request, but the cast's crit flag is still passed to addPP (apBoost 0, crit): it multiplies by the caster's critPower. The recipient's fatigue halves an originally positive gain before rounding; silence, Protect, NO_PP_GAIN and resurrecting refuse it and PP clamps at 2 x maxPP - 1; no Big Eater Belt bonus and no maxPP increase. Executed at 1 star (recipient PP 10): AP 0 request 5; AP 100 request 7.5 -> 8; AP 100 with critPower 2 and a crit 15; with fatigue also 7.5 -> 8. The caster itself gains nothing and spends its maxPP like any cast. No damage, no status.

targeting.who: all units on the board with the same team as the caster, excluding the caster (tg.id !== pokemon.id); no range, distance, targettability or alive check beyond what board.forEach yields
targeting.note: requiresTarget is false, so it can be cast without walking to a target; the target argument is null for the process. Whether board.forEach visits only living board occupants was not read.

effects.scaling: value passed to addPP = rawStarValue x (2 + AP/100) (the base is doubled before AP scaling, so AP 0 gives 2x raw). addPP is called with apBoost 0, so no further AP scaling; the cast's crit flag multiplies by critPower only if the cast crit (needs ABILITY_CRIT: canCritByDefault is false).
effects.resolution: in addPP: Math.round(value x critPower-if-crit x 0.5-if-the-ally-is-fatigued), then the Twist Band helper (a positive gain is unchanged), then the gain is skipped if the ally is silenced, protected, has NO_PP_GAIN or is resurrecting; the ally's pp is clamped to 0..(2 x maxPP - 1).

starBehavior.note: Stars of the caster index the table (1-4, fallback 20); the catalog lists these units at 1, 2 or 3 stars, so the 4-star entry (20, fallback 20) are declared in the tables but unused by the bound baseline classes.

TROP_KICK.scope: The three units in appliesTo declare TROP_KICK: Bounsweet (1 star), Steenee (2 stars), Tsareena (3 stars); all range 1, maxPP 120, no passive. The strategy is shared; unit differences are only the star count. Units not listed are not covered.
TROP_KICK.summary: Single-target. In this order: first the cast target's Attack is lowered by a requested amount of 3/5/7 (by the caster's stars; scaled by the caster's AP and crit inside addAttack and changed by the target's items), then the target takes SPECIAL damage (raw 50/100/200 by stars). The negative request is scaled by the caster's AP and crit and Math.round-ed before the recipient helpers (AP -50 turns -3 into -1.5 which rounds to -1); an enemy Big Eater Belt does not amplify it, a Twist Band holder GAINS the amount, ATK floors at 1; it does not depend on the damage landing (a protected target is still debuffed) and nothing restores it in the strategy. Executed (target ATK 20): -3 -> 17, AP 100 or a crit -> 14, Twist Band -> 23, ATK 2 -> 1.

targeting.who: the cast target only
targeting.note: No area; no other unit is touched. How the cast target is chosen in a fight was not examined.

effects.scaling: requested = table[stars-1]. handleSpecialDamage: x (1 + AP/100) (apBoost defaults to true); x critPower (reduced by Rocky Helmet / Black Augurite on the target) only if the cast crit (canCritByDefault is false, so it needs ABILITY_CRIT); x2 once with a DOUBLE_DAMAGE effect; x1.2 with STRANGE_STEAM_BOARD_EFFECT.
effects.resolution: applied = requested after those multipliers; PokemonState.handleDamage then applies attacker/field/weather multipliers, divides by (1 + ARMOR_FACTOR x speDef), rounds up with a minimum of 1 and lets the shield absorb first; the returned takenDamage is unused (core-mechanics.md section J1). The damage is dealt after the Attack debuff, which does not change it (special damage does not read the target's Attack). No heal or kill trigger follows in this strategy.

effects.scaling: requested change = -table[stars-1]. addAttack(value, caster, apBoost = 1, crit): value = Math.round(value x (1 + 1 x caster.ap / 100) x (crit ? caster.critPower : 1)), so it grows with the caster's AP and with a crit. The call passes no permanent flag.
effects.resolution: applied change differs from the request: the shared helpers then run. applyBigEaterBeltStatBuff does not scale it (a negative value from another team is not a buff for a Big Eater Belt holder). applyTwistBandBuff multiplies a negative value from another team by -1 for a Twist Band holder, so the target GAINS that much Attack instead. Finally atk = min(1)(atk + value), so Attack never drops below 1. With no items the applied change is the rounded scaled amount, limited by the floor of 1. Because permanent is false, only the in-fight entity changes; nothing in the strategy restores it.

starBehavior.note: Both tables are indexed by the casting entity's stars; the 4-star entries (400 damage, 14 attack, also the ?? fallbacks) are declared in the tables but unused by the bound baseline classes. All three units have maxPP 120 and range 1.

The raw amount is doubled (40/80/160) when status.hasNegativeStatus() is truthy at the moment of the cast: any of burn, silence, fatigue, freeze, sleep, confusion, wound, paralysis, charm, flinch, armorReduction, curse, locked, blinded or possessed is set, or poisonStacks > 0. The predicate tests flags only, no timer: a wound flag with cooldown 0 (as after clearNegativeStatus, before the next update) still doubles, cooldowns alone with the flags false do not, and negative stat changes are not statuses (all executed); the damage then goes through handleSpecialDamage (AP scaling, crit only if the cast crit, multipliers) and the target's SPE_DEF division. No status is applied and no heal/shield/buff is made.

targeting.who: the cast target passed to the strategy (the caster's current target)

effects.scaling: requested amount = raw (x2 if the target has a negative status). In handleSpecialDamage: x (1 + AP/100) (apBoost defaults to true and HEX does not pass it); x2 if the caster has DOUBLE_DAMAGE (effect is consumed); x1.2 if either side has STRANGE_STEAM_BOARD_EFFECT; the crit factor 1 + (critPower - 1) x critReductionFactor only if the cast crit (canCritByDefault is false, so it needs ABILITY_CRIT), reduced to 0 for a Rocky Helmet target and by 0.1 per Black Augurite of the target's player (floor 0)
effects.resolution: then PokemonState.handleDamage: x2 if the caster is enraged, attacker/target field and weather multipliers (read only as a list), SPE_DEF division damage / (1 + 0.05 x speDef) with speDef halved (rounded) while the target has armorReduction, Poke Doll / Guts-Sturdy-Defiant-Coaching / Wonder Guard flat or percentage reductions, then ceil with a minimum of 1; blocked entirely (takenDamage 0, no damage) by protect / skydiving / magicBounce (magicBounce also queues a reflected hit to the caster unless the caster holds Protective Pads), or if the target is at 0 hp or resurrecting. Requested amount = the raw (doubled or not) value; applied damage = what remains after these steps; the returned takenDamage is unused (core-mechanics section J1). A Cover Band ally adjacent to a target that would die takes the hit instead.

The returned takenDamage is unused (section J1).

MAGIC_BOUNCE.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare MAGIC_BOUNCE: Natu (1 star) and Xatu (2 stars); both maxPP 70, range 2, no passive. The strategy is shared; the only unit difference is the star count, which sets the bounce factor when the status later bounces damage.
MAGIC_BOUNCE.summary: Needs no target. The cast spends PP and sets magicBounce with a requested 5000 ms (a longer existing timer is kept). While it is set, handleSpecialDamage blocks EVERY attack type entering it (returned takenDamage 0, spellBlockedCount +1), but only SPECIAL damage > 0 from an attacker without Protective Pads queues a bounce 500 ms later. The delayed command calls attacker.handleDamage DIRECTLY with isRetaliation true (handleSpecialDamage is not called again) for round(factor [0.5, 1, 2, 4] x the captured raw incoming damage x (1 + holder AP/100) x (bounceCrit ? holder critPower : 1)); stars, AP and critPower are read when the callback runs. bounceCrit is the incoming crit OR a holder ABILITY_CRIT roll, so an incoming crit forces it. Callback lifecycle and death handling are not verified.

Status.update ticks the cooldown while the flag is set; the flag clears when cooldown - dt <= 0.

The captured damage is the unscaled argument of handleSpecialDamage (the block precedes its AP step).

A DelayedCommand with delay 500 calls attacker.handleDamage directly with attackType SPECIAL, attacker = holder and isRetaliation true; it does NOT call handleSpecialDamage again, so an attacker's own magicBounce does not block it. The attacker's handleDamage then applies its shared steps (core-mechanics section A); the returned takenDamage is unused (core-mechanics section J1).
